Most veggie dogs in the refrigerated section of the grocery store have a ton of onion in them!  These Veja-dogs are OK on taste, but I do not like the texture.  It is A LOT like that of a hard boiled egg white.  When I first got one out of the can I did not want to even try one.  It was squishy and had tiny dark brown spots.  The syrupy stuff they are stored in really grossed me out too.  I have eaten about 5 now and am still not crazy about them.  My son however LOVES them.  He says they are his favorite.  I will try another Worthington veggie dog (Super Links or linkettes) before giving up on the "canned" dogs all together.  I hate onions, but I prefer the texture of the tofu dogs found in the grocery store.

I ordered 24 of these burgers. It was my first time trying Omaha Steaks and I'm rather disappointed. While they do hold their shape well and cook fairly quickly, they do not have much flavor at all. Way too similar to regular supermarket frozen patties. They are a let down for the price. You'd get more texture, flavor, and value from standard ground beef. Definitely not worth $45. I'd give them 2 and a half stars if possible.

I love sardines, and I believe that the best sardines are the one from Portugal....but the one from Spain are pretty close. I bought these before, when they were made in Spain. Not anymore, now are made in Morocco, but of inferior quality compared to Season's... Definitely a big drop in quality, the flavor is different...This purchase was the last one, I will not buy them again.
alot of tas in here and  idont like tea, and i got an EMPTY CUP, 33 ot of the 35 where kosher for those of yuo wondering

In trying to eat a low-carb diet, I have tried all of this brand's chocolate bars. Of those offered the dark chocolate are definitely the best. The maltitol flavoring is certainly not as good as a normal chocolate bar, but considering it's low carb value it's not bad. The dark chocolate is naturally less sweet, and I am guessing that means it gets less of the artificial sweetener in this bar. Either way, if you like dark chocolate and need to avoid the sugar, this is a passable bar which tastes OK. I was much less enthusiastic about the other flavors (almond and coconut).

I ordered this product thinking it would be really good but it wasnt. First off its very hard chew to begin with. Second the taste is so-so; the main taste is really the taste of every generic bubble gum flavor but there is a sub taste which is actually pretty good. However, I wouldnt buy this again- in my eyes this is as bad as that regular dubble bubble chewing gum.
I found the oil a bit weak in taste. I had expected a stronger walnut flavor. I hope it is not chemically produced like most truffle oils.

I'm not giving this 5 stars, not even 4 because it lacks quality in certain areas. The tub of pretzels is basically a little bigger than a half gallon of milk. At any wholesale club, you can get the same amount of pretzels for less than half the cost without the peanut butter. The reason I bought such a large container is because I like snacking on pretzels; seeing that these have peanut butter in them, I decided to try them. On opening these peanut butter filled pretzels: quality is pretty good, nothing wow. The texture of the pretzels are soft and flavorful with a thin crunch, not bland. The peanut butter flavor within is good also, something in between Skippy and generic peanut butter. These little bite sized snacks are filling, about a dozen will hold your hunger. Though, about a dozen gets you a good part of your daily sodium, like many salted pretzels. About 10% of the pretzels in the tub came (before even opening) broken and with crumbs of pretzel bits. Well it's been a little over a month and all that remains are about five handfuls of them left stale and granulated mixed with salt. The peanut butter inside have become dehydrated but still edible.

The sunflower seeds are big and taste good.  The flavorings were not as strong and recognizable as I thought they would be.  The Spicy Garlic were my favorite.  I could not really get a good feel for the flavor on the BBQ seeds or the Ranch. I haven't tried the Dill Pickle or Salt & Pepper yet.  Overall a good sunflower seed, but I think the flavor coatings on David & Sons is much better.

I was overall disappointed with this basket.  While the salami and cheese spread were good, much of the rest of the basket seemed to be fillers.  The box of chocolates actually contained wrapped candy (a mallo cup, a peanut butter cup and some of what was once called penny candy).  There were crackers and pretzels (a small bag contained two hard pretzels).  I realize with a purchase like this you are really paying a premium for the packaging and delivery but I thought this one was a little light on actual food.

I actually feed my cats pumpkin to maintain a healthy digestive system and they love it! Unfortunately there has been a pumpkin shortage in the stores. The only canned pumpkin available was the organic at Amazon. I have never used this before. Although the cats eat it, I was disappointed because it is very "watery". I just wonder if this will impact pumpkin pies at Thanksgiving if we still have a shortage!

The Clear brand dandruff shampoos seem to be everywhere now. They use pyrithione zinc to control dandruff, similar to other brands, but cost a bit more in my experience. If they work the same for dandruff control, then they can only differentiate themselves in fragrance, texture, and cleaning.

FRAGRANCE

Typical dandruff shampoos smell medicinal, but not bad. More expensive shampoos often have really strong invigorating smells like mint. This shampoo (Strong & Full), with a price between the two extremes, also has a fragrance somewhere in the middle. It smells good, but is also very subtle.

TEXTURE

Another review nailed the texture as "melted ice cream." More importantly, it lathers well enough, though it is a bit hard to spread through long hair.

CLEANING

My hair feels clean, but not squeaky clean. It is similar to other creamy dandruff shampoos in this aspect. Conditioner is not included, and if you normally use it, you will want to use it with this product as well. My hair felt pretty dry after this alone.

OVERALL

Clear Strong & Full shampoo is a very standard shampoo, seeming to excel at being middle-of-the-road in every aspect. It will probably neither excite or disappoint you.

My two dogs get a chicken breast filet at bedtime each night.  They love them.  I have tried many different brands; they love them all.  This particular brand has one thing I really like; they are fairly uniform in size.  However, the ingredients list vegetable glycerin which I don't see the point of in a jerky type treat but also provides some carbohydrates.  This may be good or bad, depending on if you are looking for a pure protein source. The reason they get 3 stars, and the reason I probably won't buy again, is they contain salt.  Why? Other brands are only chicken breast filets with no additives.  And yes, they are made in China, but most are.  Just have to use good sense; they are a treat and should only be a small percentage of the dog's daily intake.
I've been experimenting with flavored coffees and this looked like fun. I feel it has a little bit of an artificial aftertaste but it is tolerable. Don't think I will order it again.
Pretty cool idea.  Lab loved it for a while...then it broke when it got tossed onto the driveway - bye, bye, toy!

The taste of this baby food isn't bad, and my baby likes to eat it. I wonder am I not getting the freshest shipment or this product just has a shorter shelf life than other leading brands. My order is expiring in 6 months from the day I received it.

This isn't a bad tasting product all things considered. It's reasonably refreshing, and the ingredients all look fairly healthy. However what startled me, and may actually put off a lot of people, are the bits of passion fruit floating in the tea. I realize it's a sign that they're using real fruit for their fruit flavor, but to be honest, if you've got a problem with pulp in your orange juice, you really need to steer clear of this drink.

Other than that, and without commenting on any possible health benefits from the green tea or aloe (None are made on the bottle) at 80 calories per bottle it looks like a reasonably decent alternative to soda. It's sweetened with cane sugar for those of you who are particular about your sweeteners. I'm thinking that it would make a nice summer drink for anyone who doesn't mind stray bits of fruit in their glass.

I was disappointed to find my tea bags hastily packed in a 6X6x6 shipping box, and only 93 of 100 tea bags. Also this batch of tea almost without any Jasmin taste. In the past my Stash green jasmin tea was better.

Arctic Zero's "Mint Chocolate Cookie" flavor is excellent for what it is, but it might not be what you think.  I thought that it would be a white/mint ice-cream with chocolate cookies, but it's a CHOCOATE ice-cream with mint flavoring. There are no cookies involved.  So, as long as you know what you're getting, it's still very good.  Personally, I'd like it if they came out with a traditional "mint-chip" flavor though.

I love dark chocolate, but I found this bar too bland for my tastes. It has one note of flavor and not very interesting. Funny thing is, when I handed the remaining squares out, everyone who usually only liked milk chocolate loved this bar. So if you like milk chocolate, but would like the benefits of dark chocolate, this may be the perfect compromise. However, if you like the bracing complexity of dark chocolate, you may find yourself giving this chocolate away.

I usually really like Newman products and like supporting their business, this is the first item I will not be repurchasing.

NOTE: The bars are as tall as an iPhone and a little wider than one -- just a heads up if you think this is a large bar, it is not. You will want to note the weight of the bars if using for a recipe.

We have tried many many different brands of coconut water and when we purchased this one at the store we thought it had the best taste on the market and quickly ordered a case. The box arrived in great condition but, as many reviewers have noted, every single can was dented and scratched. On top of that, it didn't taste nearly as good as the ones we had purchased at the grocery store. I don't know if the dents would have altered the taste but there was definitely a difference. While still drinkable, we probably won't order again.
I didn't expect so many flavored coffee cups. I would like to have a Krazy Kup package with no flavored ones.

Firstly, I don't eat Indian food often so I'm absolutely no expert on Indian cuisine. I've always enjoyed palak paneer at Indian restaurants so I thought I'd give this a try. Each packet contained a decent amount of cheese - about the amount shown in the picture, and the cheese is pretty good. The spinach sauce is very watery, like pureed spinach soup, but still flavorful. It was more spicy-hot than what I've had in restaurants, which I didn't like. Overall - I liked the cheese, didn't like the sauce.

Any steel cut oats are better than than instant or rolled oats, but among steel cut oats, McCann's are not the best.  I enjoyed McCann's until I saw their prices increasing, which encouraged me to try other options.  Bob's Red Mill steel cut oats are just as satisfying, filling, and beneficial, but with a MUCH lower price.  In addition, Bob's won the world porridge competition last year.  So perhaps you will agree that they also have a better taste!

We were disappointed with the light, mild flavor and the thin liquidy syrup.  For a premium priced product, we expected something better than we bought at Costco, but this was not to our taste.  Sorry.

When folks give this a 5 star, they MUST be basing it on the taste of low carb bread. As far as breads go (Fresh made Italian being the best), this does not compare. However, if you want an edible bread that is very filling, this will fit the bill. Don't confuse this with really good tasting bread, it isn't. But it serves its purpose!

Form: bottle-cap size pressed cakes, dark color. Opens to medium-sized leaves. Looks to be at least somewhat tippy. Could be wrong about that, though.
Color: Dark as coffee, but with a more reddish tone. Quite pretty actually.
Smell: smoke and some faint sweetness.
Tate: Very assertive. Dry hay dust. Wet mulch. Smoke. Long-lingering smokey/woody after-taste.

I bought this because I wanted something "earthy" and bold, and boy did I get it in spades! It's pleasant enough and a nice change of pace from my normal Ceylon routine. I don't know how well it rates within the black pu-erh family, but my uneducated opinion is that I'm not sure I could see myself drinking this every day. The woody aspect is overwhelming at times. Maybe a couple times a month when I'm in the mood for something a lil' "dirty." If you are on the fence, I say give it a shot!

Lozano is wonderful salsa. In costa rica it is the condiment on every table. It's unique flavor is a fun change to other as
Was.

I like it ok, but it isn't anything great. I have a hot water tap and it is just as easy for me to make the powder packs at home at a fraction of the cost. I'll go back to that method and save my $$ for coffee.

Nutritionally, I thought these bars were fine. 140 calories, 3 grams fat, 4 grams fiber, 9 grams sugar.  The ingredients were recognizable and include apple puree, banana puree and dried pumpkin.  Unfortunately, the taste is not very appealing.  The chocolate is barely discernable and the taste of the rest of the bar is lackluster.  It may be because although the bars use decent ingredients, there are a lot of them and it must be highly processed.  Despite my lack of enthusiasm, my 4-year-old liked these bars just fine.  So 2 stars from mom and 4 stars from the kid make for a 3 star rating.

I have tried enough natural type bars to fill a health food store and without a doubt this is one of the best all around bars, but it is far from perfect. Great taste, but they melt easily during a hot spell or while travelling. But here's the real problem: First the bar uses non-GMO soy isolate (!!!!) as a protein source which many experts believe will alter your hormones profile by lowering testosterone and raising estrogen . . . exactly what a fitness enthusiast or person seeking longevity would not want. It also contains licorice which is on the possible list of supplements that can lower T. Even though the bar has an alkaline ph you might experience heartburn due to the soy isolate. Is it possible the licorice was added to combat the GERD/heartburn as well as enhance the taste? Perhaps, but at what cost?

On the positive side I'm not sure I could name a better bar or better tasting bar overall, and again I've tried them all. Most taste terrible or are loaded up with fake sugars like Stevia (billed as being healthy) which a lot of people just can't digest very well.

I love the idea of a dog biscuit that will freshen your doglies breath. I have 5, so I'm always trying different dental bones and things to help me out there. These bones are the perfect size, smell great~~like human food, actually~~but out of 5 dogs, only 2 would eat them. I actually put one in my youngest dog, Tobey's mouth, and tried to coax him. He spit it back out!! Not sure if it was the smell, or the taste, but I hate to report that it would be a waste of money for me to buy these. I have 4 Lhasa Apsos, and a Schneagle~~the Lhasa's I do have to say are pretty picky eaters, and 3 of them are the ones who wouldn't touch them, so take that as you will.
I WISH they loved them so that they COULD Crunch n' Clean!!

Way overpriced for a 16 oz. cake. I'm a baker so for me this is just okay. When I bake, it's butter, eggs, sugar, flour, etc. There are too many artificial ingredients in this cake, making it taste processed. Just get yourself a good pound cake or yellow cake recipe (please, no boxed cake mix), and make a rum syrup. That's it. Let it soak, soak, soak and you'll have a better and more natural tasting cake. The up side though, it's cheaper to purchase on Amazon than direct from the Tortuga factory.
Don't be like I did, and buy them thinking they were chocolate flavored cigars, their just chocolate candy. Cool looking yes, but candy non the less.

I must state up front that I am not much of a fruity candy lover. That being said, the Pomegranate Licorice is pretty good. You can taste the fruit, but you also get the anise flavor. That is an important distinction as my wife, who loves similar products, didn't like these due to the anise. I personally liked them BECAUSE of the anise flavor.

I didn't care for the fact that the number one ingredient is wheat, but beyond that it appears to be a quality product.

This Crystal Light "mojito" flavored drink mix is okay as far as I'm concerned.

The flavor is very different and unusual...not to be found everywhere...and for that I give extra points.

The flavor is like a Mojito--I'd prefer a little more mint ...but the lime taste is there.

Needs ice in the glass for best flavoring......but on a warm day...sit in a comfortable chair...with a tall ice filled glass.............

On that day this drink is a little slice of heaven.

While I would not list this as my top flavor---- but to break up the monotony of my grape or strawberrys.. I like that change that it brings to the table.

I was expecting better. The broth is decent and the beans are pretty good, but the vegetables are too soft and overcooked and there's not enough of them. Progresso Minestrone low-sodium soup is much better, but it has egggs and milk which I can no longer eat since I'm vegan. By the way I contacted Amazon via email last week to remove the gluten-free description on this soup. I guess someone fell asleep at customer service because I never got a reply nor has the description been rectified. Like I said, I expected better.

Addendum, October 19, 2012: Amazon finally acted on my request to remove the gluten-free description on the soup. The soup is no longer labeled as gluten-free. Thank you Amazon.
I love these things! But often the bags are not sealed, making freshness a big issue. Let the company know that the bags often unseal. Or find a different distributor of non-wheat sesame sticks.

This is NOT the same good Matzo Farfel you are used to from Manischewitz it is in a new container.  Each can only holds 14 oz instead of the 16 oz we are used to.  The container is Taller and Narrower with new images but the product is NOT identical ---  this product is lower quality AND there are 2 oz less product per can at approximately the same price as before.  If it were the same product (which it is NOT) --- it would be a very good value when purchased from Amazon LLC using Amazon Prime Free Shipping.  Very disappointed.

I was looking for something to drink that would replace my coffee occasionally.  This is okay, but doesn't mix with hot water.  I actually meant to get the vanilla latte flavor, but ordered the wrong one. It also has less protein in it than most protein drinks. It's alright, not my favorite.

Yes, these gluten free cookies are absolutely delicious! There's just no getting around that. As I was munching my absolutely delicious cookie I had a look-see at the Nutrition Facts printed on the wrapper - that's when I had my second "WOW!".
ONE cookie is TWO servings - when was the last time you cut a cookie in half? So....if you are glutinous enough to eat your entire cookie at one time, you have consumed 340 calories (100 are fat calories)and 40 mg. of cholesterol. I was astounded to say the least. As someone with a gluten allergy, I can tell you that there are other really good cookies out there without these kinds of overloads. Try the Glutino sandwich cookies, for example.
3 out of the 6 were in the melted stage, the Chocolate Peanut Butter had a good flavor, I did not like the plain Chocolate. I will not order this again...

I tried some of this tea yesterday evening.  I have been battling adrenal and hypothyroid problems and getting much better through the use of natural glandulars (Armor thyroid is natural, as is cortef) products and many supplements and healthy life choices in general.  Last night and today, after the tea, I felt awful.  My morning underarm temp had dropped significantly and I just feel cold in general. I have been weak and tired and shaky all day, though at first I did not know why. Should have researched more first, but like most teas oolong tea has flouride and that is bad for a hypothyroid condition.  I can't guarantee the tea is the reason for the downturn, but it is something to think about if you get it and feel the same way. I am giving this product 3 stars because it came quickly, was nicely boxed and tastes fine.
The box had been opened before and was taped with Scotch tape Several of the kcups were leaking into the box and had to be tossed That is the first time that has happened but I was very disappointed.

In the world of brew-at-home chai, you have the purists who watch for spice sales ("Oooh, oooh, I found star anise in the bargain bin at Vons!") and people like me who are just looking for a more exotic version of English breakfast tea with milk.

The Higgins & Burke Chai was alright. If my supermarket choice was this, Tazo or Good Earth, I'd get this in a second.

However, unlike other brands I buy frequently, you can't really see the individual pieces of spices (cardamom pods, arms of star anise). I prefer the more premium teas that have identifiable spices. I did notice more spice/tea dust than usual inside the envelope. More finely powdered teas lose their flavor quicker than the more chunky stuff.

If homemade/authentic restaurant chai is a 10, Good Earth a 1, I'd give this a solid 4. (Two Leaves and a Bud Black Chai is an 8, Bombay Chai is a 8, Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf is a 6, Stash Double Spice is 6, Tazo is a 3, Bigelow/Twinings are 1s, any premade chai liquid/powder with sugar is a -3).

Numi made with Roobios doesn't count on the scale.

Let me first say that this is a delicious tea. My problem is that the ginger in it isn't a strong one, and I feel a tea with Ginger in the title should at least taste like it more.

I had the choice of buying either the Republic of Tea's Orange Spice for a few cents more than this flavor. The Orange Spice was an herbal tea listed as a digestion aid, while the Pineapple Ginger is a daily green tea. I'm disappointed in this flavor. I wanted a tea like Stash's Lemon Ginger, that really gives you good strong ginger taste. The reason I bought the ROT Pineapple Ginger is because I was driving all around town and couldn't find the Stash. Took a chance on it, because I usually like Republic of Tea's products, even though they're pricey.

Well, I'll keep it because green tea is good for me, but I guess I'll just have to find the Stash Lemon Ginger online. Would the Orange Spice have been more satisfying to me? Don't know. Expensive lesson on this one.

I bought this sauce hoping to be able to make Pad Thai for my family at home that would taste similar to what we get when we eat out. I know that recipes and tastes will vary from one to the next, but this was listed as "Classic Thai sauce".

The first night I tried using it, I immediately knew it wasn't what I was looking for. Luckily I had Thai Kitchen, Pad Thai Sauce on hand and between the two I was able to come up with something that my family did enjoy.

While this sauce may be a starting point for your meal, if you're like me it won't be enough. While I was hoping to find something pre-made and easy, I may just need to get up enough courage to try making it from scratch.

I loved this as a kid and the core flavour is still the same but I never noticed the after-taste of artificial sweetener before.  Still enjoyed the drink but the after-taste got to me eventually. Might have to risk the rotten teeth and back-fat and just get the full sugar one next time...or maybe even go all out and get some ribena

I haven't been having quality issues like some of the others. However I really don't care for the Fuhgeddaboutit flavor. It tastes like cheap instant coffee. Very ashy and bland.

6/15/12 Update:
Thank you Brooklyn Bean for the excellent response and the variety box. After tasting all the flavors I've determined that I just don't like the dark roasts from Brooklyn Bean. I like the medium and light roasts.

However I am getting a lot of grounds in my cup from quite a few of these. Our commercial machines at work really don't like these for some reason.

The best apple juice products are processed directly from harvest. This stuff is reconstituted from concentrate with pureed skins apparently mixed in, but the result is watery and lacks fresh apple juice richness of taste. You can't tell this from the bottles which are heavily tinted, but poured into a glass it is pale and lacks body, even after vigorous shaking. Not looking forward to going through 8 gallons, wish I had bought just one at the store first.

The milk is "creamy" and tastes nice. No complaints on this front. However, WholeFoods sells organic almond milk for a lot less. This product is great to have in the pantry but I would not be buying frequently from Amazon.
for the money its not as good as others its also very sweet for being suger free the size is very small i should of read more about it a normal granola is double the size of these

I got this honey because I thought it is different from what you get from walmart but actually its taste and smell is  the same and if you are looking for something that tastes and smells like real honey it is not yours.
didn't get ,quite the taste i wanted,brought thru amazon. but overall will still keep using this product,until it runs out.

Extract of tea leaves doesn't impress me, but results do.  Unfortunately, I don't really see any difference after using this shampoo vs. the cheap stuff from Wallyworld.  Admittedly, my hair is very short so there isn't much 'result' to notice but I would think it should do something different.  Everyone's hare is different so if this stuff interests you try it out.  For me, it didn't do much.

The Izze all natural Pomegranate drink is a great idea. A Natural drink with no artificial sweeteners or even refined sugar. Best of all, no corn syrup. It sounds like a nice healthy drink, right? Well, the reality is that it just didn't taste very good to me. And, although it claims to have 70 percent juice... most of the juice isn't Pomegranate juice.

Here's the rundown:

Pros:

-All Natural
-No refined sugar or corn syrup added
-70 percent juice content
-Fortified with vitamins

Cons:

-Doesn't taste good. Sour, bitter, and tastes more like wine than juice.
-Most of the juice isn't pomegranate... it's a mix of apple, pear...etc
-Isn't sweet enough... they could have used raw sugar, I wouldn't mind.

Conclusion:

I just didn't like the taste of it. It may be more healthy for you than most other drinks... but if it doesn't taste good, what's the point? I expected it to taste like pomegranate, and it totally didn't. There's not even much pomegranate juice in it. Though, if you are into wine, you may like it. It tastes more like wine than juice.

My dog **loved** this food. As soon as she smelled it she started barking at me, as I poured it into her bowl. One of my elderly cats even sidled up and tried to steal some of the dog food, and a small food fight erupted momentarily. So for palatability this rates high! I could see this being a successful food for a pet who just normally is not enthusiastic at eating.

But let's break it down: the main composition of this dog food? Soy, rice, corn, wheat. If my dog weren't a carnivore, I'd be ok with this. But my dog has allergies, big time, and this food is mostly filler in my opinion. I feed her Blue Buffalo Wilderness (no grain) or else she will develop a bad smell, itch, and have lots of scabs and skin problems.

At the end of the day I would recommend this to someone instead of Ol' Roy or some cheap store brand food, but overall I don't like that most of the ingredients are filler grains. I would not feed this unless I absolutely had to. At least I would know that my pets would scarf it down!

I had some delicious pumpkin cereal that I bought at a gourmet market last fall. Since it was a seasonal item, they no longer have it. Hoping this was similar, I took a chance. It is not pumpkin-y at all. I guess the "pumpkin" comes from adding pumpkin seeds to tasteless raisin bran. This cereal also has a lot of calories, about 220 per serving. That's pretty high compared to tasteless raisin bran. Now I have 6 boxes of this stuff. What to do?

Prior to the last few orders, I hadn't run into problems with the packing. On the last canned Friskies cat food orders, I get poorly packed boxes and dented as well as popped open cans which I then have to throw away and clean off the mess on the other cans. The product is good, whoever is packing isn't doing a good job.
The product was delicious.  However, we sent it as a gift and there was no way to put a gift card because it didn't actually come from Amazon.  I won't order again without a way to attach gift card.
My husband is a coffee drinker.  He finds this coffee just ok...nothing great.  For those who needs low acid coffee, this is probably not a bad choice.

I've used this seller before and have always had an excellent experience, but i've never ordered this particular color of luster dust before, and i appear to have picked the wrong shade.  This moonstone color is very dark, does not have hardly any shine, and i had to use half the jar to get a visible shade.  i can't think of anything i can use it for - i'm doing some tombstones this month, maybe this will be the right shade for that, but i like the brilliant silver much better.  Also, i almost broke my teeth getting the little jars open - now i use pliars.

The Grape Jam, itself, is of the highest quality, and it tastes great, so I have absolutely no complaints there. However, the glass jars were poorly packaged (it was very heavy and fragile, and was insulated with just two small pillow puffs), and two of the twelve jars arrived with the seals already broken. Since I could not be sure if the food was safe to eat, I had to throw away the two jars. I would not order this product again(or anything else that comes in jars) for that reason.

I used to use Tassimo, and switched to Keurig when Starbucks went to Keurig (it's all family members drink).  Compared to other Starbucks blends, this one tastes less bitter, "smoother" perhaps.  I'll stop short of saying "watery," but it isn't quite strong enough for my first cup.

These cookies are reasonably tasty without being too sweet. The individual packing keeps them nice and moist and makes it easy to include one in a packed lunch.

That said, they are not so special that I'd make an effort to seek them out. Also, the fact that each cookie is 170 calories would keep me from having them too often. Luckily, the individual packing will keep them fresh till you feel like having one.

Flat, flavorless, weak. Don't bother unless you like your coffee really weak. I'd guess a fair description would be using 4 tablespoons of coffee in a regular coffee maker with water for 8 5oz cups. I'm looking for my Tassimo manual to see if there's a way to reduce the water used so I could perhaps get a half-cup of decaf at an acceptable strength.

REVISED:
I found the manual. Simply push the start/stop button after brewing has started to stop the process earlier (making the coffee stronger). At 2/3 cup, the strength is just about right. I now rate this product 3 stars.

bacon sunflower seeds... sounds great, right? well i thought so too... but they put a little too much baconsalt on them, crazy right? but the paprika or whatever it is overpowers everything else & because of that i can only eat 3-4 seeds at atime.. big disappointment.

So I'm a big fan of Rock Star Energy Drinks . . .Well . .Let me specify . .I'm a big fan of the Original Rock Star Energy Drink (Citrus-flavored). Why? Because it pumps me up AND it tastes wonderful. This, Double-Energy crud, may pump me up even more (which is not exactly the best thing when I'm just about to go to class),but it tastes awful . .It tastes like that horrible cough medicine that was given to you as a kid.  ... Yes . . . It's THAT bad . . .So,unless you REALLY need the energy, I'd suggest sticking to the original . . .

The product I received was fine, but the Supplier(Eray) was impossible to deal with.  I saw that shipping on $50.00 was to be free, only to be charged almost one-third again for shipping cost.  I feel that these people robbed me and no-one cared.  I will not do business with Amazon again do to this.

Mrs. Leeper's Beef Stroganoff is blandly adequate but uninspiring.  Even after I added a liberal dose of cayenne, I could barely taste it.  It's okay as a vehicle for the protein in the beef and the riboflavin in the noodles, especially if you can't digest wheat gluten.  But it has even less flavor than Hamburger Helper, if you can imagine such a thing.  When the best I can say is that it's handy and not unpleasent, that's a thin recommendation.

Kool Aid's been around for 85 years and most folks have tried it at some time so I'm reviewing the flavor not the idea that it is Kool Aid versus other drink choices. The flavor is called peach mango but it is the mango that dominates the drink. As a family who loves peaches and likes mango, it seemed like a good fit but it really should be called Mango with a hint of Peach.  So, if you love mango-flavored foods and drinks you'll enjoy this. If you are looking for the peach flavor to be equal (or more because it is first in the title)to the mango then you'll be disappointed.  Also, using the directed amount exactly made the flavor taste a bit "thin"; adding a couple of teaspoons to the directed amount improved the richness of the flavor but didn't change it from mango to more of a peach-mango pair.

I had high expectations but am riding the fence about it so far.  It's syrupy which is okay except it doesn't dissolve in iced tea.  In hot tea, it leaves somewhat of a strange taste.  I've used it on my morning cereal by putting it on the cereal before adding the milk and it seems to work.  Maybe I just need to get used to it but, so far, it's a slow process.  There weren't any guidelines on how to use it and that probably would have been helpful.  I'll continue to try using it, though, until I'm fully convinced one way or the other.
I did a search on Vegan Gummy Bears and these came up pretty high on the list - they are NOT Vegan. They have gelatin(made from cow or pig hooves) in them.

I like Oreos, but I didn't care for this incarnation.  The Peanut Butter Fudge Creme Oreo has only one very thin cookie, not the sandwich we associate with traditional Oreos.  On top of that is peanut butter and the whole thing is dipped in chocolate.  Peanut butter and chocolate usually blend well for me, but this was just too sweet and I needed more of that cookie bite.  I shared it with a large playgroup yesterday and got some positive comments but no wows.  My husband says he'll eat them if they're there, but he wouldn't go out of his way to buy them.

I thought I was buying this in lbs, not ounces.  It is a very small bag and very expensive!  Too expensive to make this my cats dry food choice.  The cats liked it okay, but they weren't in love with it, so I didn't purchase again.
This cereal is really good, but the price keeps going up and the boxes keep getting smaller. I like that some of the money goes to good causes, but unfortunately I had to switch to a cheaper brand.

I almost wonder if my oil is spoiled?  Was expecting a buttery warm taste with some bite..and it's off. I know the quality of what Ina prefers from her books and show and this doesn't seem up to par...

I have loved making Jiffy Pop since I was a kid and have since made it a point to share the fun with my own 2 children. It is getting almost impossible to find this stuff so I was really glad to find it here. I eagerly placed an order back at the end of July 2008.

My order arrived quickly and was packaged nicely. I was super excited to see so much yummy jiffy pop all in one box. Upon closer examination however, I realized that the expiration date was the first week of October 2008. My kids and I love Jiffy Pop but making/eating 24 servings in just a little over 2 months was going to be an impossible task! I ended up giving several of them away to friends and family before they became too stale to eat.

So the deal was great and I will likely try again but just be sure to ask about the expiration date before you order so you ensure that you get that great *fresh* Jiffy Pop taste!
I liked the candy just fine ( a blast from my past), but the cost of shipping/handling was disproportionate.  I won't be making another purchase from you again any time soon.

I ate shredded beef jerky chew years ago when a friend gave me a can. I liked it and it was pretty good so I thought I'd buy some. Despite the positive reviews I got a mixed bag. It turned out 42% (or 5 out of 12 cans) of the Teriyaki beef chew was bad, I don't know if they tried to slip in some old expired jerky to pull a fast one to cut losses or a bad batch was mixed in. By bad I mean it tasted like saw dust in your mouth and wood chips, when jerky chew tastes like saw dust with bits of wood chips it isn't jerky anymore. Eating the bad jerky is like putting sand in your mouth or better yet ashes or even sand paper. I did however buy a roll of the Hickory (black cans) and a roll of Spicy (red cans) and those were better in my experience. To know if you have a bad can shake the can and if it sounds like a lot of pebbles are rolling around in the can then you got a bad can that will taste like saw dust. If I wanted sand in my mouth I would've went to the beach.

-Pros-
I only got 7 good cans
The good cans tasted like I expected it to taste

-Cons-
Got 5 bad cans
The bad cans taste like saw dust & wood chips
I had to feed the bad cans to the dog

Looks like Buffalo Bill was able to give me the slip on the Wild West Trail and swapped the good jerky I was suppose to get with saw dust. My recommendation, avoid the Teriyaki unless you want saw dust in your mouth and pick up the Spicy and Hickory flavors instead. I have a hunch that no one buys the Teriyaki flavors, that would explain why almost half of the ones I bought were bad. Would I buy this again in the future? Probably not.

I obtained a sample and when I opened the package the aroma was not inviting at all.  Well, I brewed it up anyway on a regular Cuisinart coffee maker and used the sample bag with enough water for 2-3 cups to make a stronger cup of coffee. Nevertheless, it tasted weak to me and didn't smell any better after brewing it. It was drinkable and ok, just not very satisfying to me as it didn't have a richness or depth or good aroma to it. Admittedly, I am not a big French Roast fan as it tends to taste bitter to me and acidic.  This one may be better than other French Roast because while I thought it tasted weak and bitter it presumably is lower acid. If you need a low acid coffee, then this is okay, but if not you may not find this satisfying, especially if you like dark, full flavored strong coffee.

I bought these for my husband.  He is a marathon runner.  He was disappointed that they were not higher in calories.  I think these are good for runners that are running 1/2 marathons or training for similar mileage.  They are not high enough in calories for marathon training.

Great product by Iams but my two mini pinschers would not eat it until they were starving.  I had them on the yellow package puppy Iams and they seemed to like that more.  Don't get me wrong the product is solid with healthy ingredients but my dogs just wouldn't take it.

I wanted to love this coffee. The service on the Caffe Bombard coffee was fine, but I really expected more Italian 'oomph' in the roast. the write up says "Ambrosial Aroma, Great Body, Delicious Flavor, Long lasting Finish" and honestly it's not quite there. The aroma is great, the body is a bit weak as is the flavor.

I know that northern roasts are more subdued than southern Italian, but this is quite mild. While the beans make a decent cup of espresso especially for an afternoon cup, it doesn't stand up to the milk/foam in a latte or cappuccino. My most demanding customer, my wife, says that she can't find the coffee amongst the milk. Like I said I do enjoy a straight espresso using the beans, but I also like to enjoy the occasional latte, and this doesn't cut it. Perhaps I should have realized it before purchasing. And now I have a kilo of the beans that will not be fresh by the time I should be finishing them up. Oh well. It would be valuable if the beans were offered in a smaller quantity to try out.

I love coconut and I bought this treat for that reason.  But I am not tasting the coconut.  Another person stated that there wasn't much coconut flavor to this product. I guess I should have listen more closely to what they had to say.  I like sesame too, so this treat is OK, but it is NOT what I really wanted.

These 12 oz bags are being sold at TJ Max for 5.99, and I bought two. Just tasted my first brew... Like another reviewer said, this is not the typical flavor offered from the dark selection like french roast, sumatra, etc. It's a different sensation, one I'll have to get used to because I have two bags. It still has that strong burnt-like roast taste but with different undertones. Taste is subjective. You may like it. For me, it's not an instant hit!

So my baby doesn't seem to like them. I think they would be fine and seem like a nice gluten free snack but according to my son's taste buds they don't particularly go well with him. Again I think they would be good especially as an option for gluten free snacks.

I found the illy issimo Caffe Espresso flavored coffee drink to be drinkable but it is not a drink I plan to consume on any sort of a regular basis.

While the drink does have an espresso-like taste, it is too bitter and watery to be worth over $2 for a 6.8 oz can. Further, its espresso flavor is just acceptable, nothing special. In addition to my considering this product to be just an average, at best, drink, I found it gave me such a strong caffeine jolt that for over an hour after finishing it I had a bit of a pressure headache.
Not quite as good as advertised.  The chocolate flavor has a chemical taste and the coconut seems a bit off.
I just paid $3.00 for the 6 oz tin so watch the pricing....you can still get it for a bit cheaper here but only if you purchase the large multi pack
Coffee had average flavor.  Probably would not order again.  Will continue to taste different brands until I taste a 5 star rating.
I bought this stuff thinking it was going to be hot. I did not like the taste.  It has a very sweet taste but it does have a slight afterburn.

I like this product, really I do.  Yes, I do notice that it acts like a little "pick me up" when I drink it.  Nothing drastic, but it's there and the feeling is pleasant.  Having said that, the price is just too much.  It's a drink, not medicine and I can probably find similar ingredients in a supplement for less money.  Drop the price, guys, and you will get more buyers!

I have tried all the flavors by Bear Naked and I admit they do taste terrific. I'm not too fond of the Banana cereal but the rest are pretty good. The granola is done just right...not too hard, not sweet at all, and nice and chunky!

My only gripe is that after it goes down, it lays very heavily on my stomach causing a terrible heartburn that lingers for hours. I thought it was just my body but my son has been eating it too and just this morning he asked me if it makes me feel sick. I said "not sick, but I do have indigestion." He said that must be what he is feeling.

We both say it tastes great but I think it's good to use just a few tablespoons at a time, like just add it to yogurt, not to eat as a bowl of cereal. It's just too heavy.

If it weren't for that awful feeling afterwards, I would definitely have given this product five stars based on taste and excellent granola-type consistency.
Be warned - if you are looking for real tea with balck current - this is not it

They are gooey, and they are mega--maybe to a fault. While not usually one to criticize abundance, I think Chips Ahoy! Megafudge crosses the line from welcome bounty to "too much a good thing."

Now...if you consider snacking an extreme sport, if your fudge tolerance has been built up over years of indulgance--then Megafudge might be just your thing. But we think the average chocolate lover will consider this overkill.

But no one can say they weren't warned. The product delivers what the name promises!

In the box you get yer dried elbow macaroni, an envelope of "seasoning," and an envelope of squishy Velveeta "cheese sauce."

The box is a bit of a deception, as the contents easily would fit in a smaller box. A bigger box conveys the expectation of a bigger end-product, right? And of course a bigger box stands out better on the store shelf and offers a lot more copy space for that crucial moment when you have to engage and convince the consumer. Mmmmm, pretty golden-yellow colors, and red cursive-y lettering, with a photo of noodles as big as my fingers...

I followed the on-box instructions explicitly. Well, okay, I admit it, I used 1.37 pounds of hamburger instead of the stated 1 pound. All glory and praise to Odin that there were no adverse effects! It all turned out just fine, basically just like the photo on the front of the box, neither watery/runny nor dry; everything glommed together just right. The stated "makes about 5 one-cup servings" is about right. Now, Kraft came out with the "family size" macaroni n' cheez kit way back when, and I'd argue that Velveeta (a Kraft brand) would want to do the same thing, and it might even help actually fill up this oversized/underutilized box.

I didn't add anything to the recipe, as this was the first time with the product, and I was cooking with this review in mind. As for taste, it was just fine. Nothing special, but not bad. Now, did this taste like "ultimate cheeseburger?" No, not at all. That's because there was no bun, mayonnaise, pickles, mustard, or grill-charred meat with a slick slab of melted cheez atop, all of the things I put on a cheezburger. I did go with the "customize it!" advice on the back of the box and had some chopped onions, diced tomatoes and chopped lettuce on hand, which was a nice addition to the product, more than anything lending it some crunch, and a nicer range of flavor. One could really go nuts and drop some salsa into the mix, or even saute' some fresh broccoli or carrots with the hamburger. Now we're talking a meat n' cheez dinner creation that's a lot more interesting and certainly more tasty.

If I were to use this product again--and this might be a good thing to put in the copy on the package--I'd cook some diced onions with the hamburger, and/or some chopped mushrooms. This would bulk up the servings somewhat, and definitely yield more depth of flavor. I added no spices to the product, and it was accordingly bland. If I were to cook this again, I'd add salt, pepper, some caraway seeds, maybe a bit of rosemary and most definitely some garlic and a little bit of red pepper.

Yes, it was ready in about twenty minutes, as the box copy promised.

Yes, I'd use this product again, but I can't say I'm going to go out of my way at the store to find it and buy it.

I do like the TV ads for this product, though, funny and original. Let the smiting continue!

Bottom Line: this is another offering in the great American Hamburger Helper tradition. It's a one-pan dinner that's really easy to make and takes little time. Following the instructions yields a passable main dish that while not bad, isn't really that interesting and offers some nutritional value. The kit does offer, however, a foundation upon which one can experiment and improvise to create more varied mealtime indulgences.

I love my coffee and I order my own from a coffee dealer. I usually grind my own beans for the freshest taste. I was anxious to try the Melitta Cafe when I saw it was available. I understand that there are other Melitta blends besides the lighter French style that I received.

My reaction to French roast coffee was reaffirmed when I tried this coffee. That slightly burnt, bitter taste was there and, while it was minimized somewhat, I found myself disappointed. I had that for my morning coffee and my afternoon coffee and I was going to do the same the next day. However, I decided that I really didn't want any more of the Melitta so I switched back to the coffee I had been drinking before. I think that those who like Franch roast coffee will enjoy this product. As for me, I will pass. But, hey, what do I know. I mean, I still have most of the Blue Mountain coffee I bought in Jamaica sitting on the shelf because I didn't it was all that great.

There are foods that are so good, you eat them even if they're bad for you.  Then there are foods you have to kind of force yourself to eat because you know they're healthy.  This bar leans toward the latter type.  If you took strawberry oatmeal, mixed in some wheat germ for added grainy texture and somehow got it congeal/solidify into a bar these would be the end result.  True, I don't find them as inedible as a Soyjoy bar (which can only be described as flavored, pressed sawdust).  These are a dense, filling and portable nutrition bar not to be mistaken for a treat.  I'm going to put the rest of mine in the car for emergency rations should I ever get stuck in an inordinately long traffic jam...or maybe a snowdrift.

I tried both the cookie and the cake from this mix.  The cake was dry and had a flat taste.  It did not taste like a normal yellow or white cake at all. I had to use lots of frosting to get this cake to stick together somewhat on my fork.  As for the cookies, they were extremely crumbly and fell apart the minute you bit into it.  I have several mixes left that I am going to experiment with to try to get them moister. Covering after baking normally works for regular cakes to retain moisture, but did not for this mix. If you can stand the crumblies, the cookies did taste good.

I have to start this out by saying that I am a huge fondue snob and I have always made it from scratch.  Culture Magazine, Boska and Emmi sent me some Emmi premade Fondue packs and I was really curious as to whether or not they would be any good.  I was actually surprised.  It was easy to prepare (just heat in a saucepan).  Nice, creamy texture.  And while the cheese flavor was nice, I thought it was very "alcoholly" (if that's a word).  Would I buy it again?  Maybe...if I really needed fondue and just didn't have time to grate cheese.

I was very anxious to try these graham crackers which seemed healthier that the Honey Maid brand we have purchased in the past.
Once we opened the box, we found that the crackers were broken into loads of small pieces. Despite this the had a decent taste, albeit a bit dry, but not bad with a cup of coffee or something to wash them down with.

We were pleased with the recycled packaging, but there was nothing exceptional about these crackers. Again, good enough, but we probably would not purchase these in the future unless they were available at a really terrific price.
I was not impressed with these bars.  I actually bought them by mistake.  I thought I was buying the ones with nuts.  I wouldn't buy them again.

I was a little disappointed with this collection.  It came in a shipping box as if the different pods were just thrown in there according to the combination described online.  When I read it was a "collectors" edition, I assumed more care would be taken in the packaging and the packaging itself would be special. Instead it's just a print that they put in with the coffee -- it's a black and white print that isn't any better quality than your regular poster.  The coffee itself is as described (although there are so many "bold" flavors that I'm not sure how they can claim this is a medium roast collection).  If you are looking to sample different brands and types of coffee, this works.  However, being new to Keurig brewing, I'm not sure if this is price comparable and if it costs more for the special "limited edition" package for this collection, I'd skip it as it's not worth the additional cost.
This is pretty good on tacos or as a dipping sauce.  It's not too hot and is creamy and thick.
I normally buy these crystals from another company, but decided to try these because of price. They were okay, but high in sugar and not as potent as the other brand.
Looking for a real blast? try Zombie Blast. this is really a awesome drink with nice packaging. I don't normally don't use energy drink but it works for me.

The product arrived very quickly and looked like what I had ordered.  After reading an article in the Whole Dog Journal regarding rawhide quality, I was searching for the specific brands made in the USA out of one-piece thick rawhides hand rolled cleaned without chemical.  The description of the ad led me to believe this is what I was ordering.  After giving one to my dog, I soon found this was not the quality I had ordered.  It was not one piece as the end would indicate.  They had small pieces hidden inside which is one of the choking items article warned against.  I would not say the word "Premium" is correct...perhaps "Good" is more appropriate.

I'm not much of a coffee drinker. I've had a few cold coffee drinks here and there, but I love coffee ice cream and candies. I decided to give this cappuccino drink by illy issimo a chance since I've been trying a few new things lately (like how I had Doritos for the first time last week in my nearly 27 years of existence). My initial reaction was that it didn't taste very good, but again, that's probably because I don't drink coffee very much. But after a few sips, I got used to it. I'm not saying it tasted good by any means, but it's certainly not the worst thing I've drank this year. Coffee fans will either love or hate this, depending on their personal preferences.

The nutrition info listed on the can is a bit reassuring, since this drink isn't that bad for you, and you get a little bit of protein too. It's fairly low in sugar for a drink like this too. And while it's not advertised as an energy drink, I actually felt upbeat for an hour or two after finishing the can...something I can't say for other drinks I've had like Mountain Dew or Jarritos.

I'm giving it 3 stars because it's just plain ok in my book. 'nothing special, but not terrible. It's still weird drinking coffee from a can though. Would I recommend it to anyone? Probably not, unless they could only choose between this and Diet Pepsi.

I really do like the taste of this salt, but even having read the reviews of it's moisture content, I had hope based on the product description that I would in fact be able to use it in my salt grinder.  Nope.  It just sticks to the base of the grinder.  I like the flavor so I'm scooping it out of a pyrex storage container now, but it's quite inconvenient.

I really wanted these to work for travels where I pack all my own food.  However, they are a fairly poor alternative for travels, since some of the fruit dissolves into very messy powder.  I also just couldn't get into the astronaut-food taste.  Even though it is totally real, it tastes artificial to me in this texture (unlike the blueberry flavor which is, however, even far messier than the strawberry flavor).  The quality and ripeness of the strawberries is consistent, however.  They are probably good for you if you want a stowaway fruit you can use when you haven't gotten to the store for awhile or want it out of season to sprinkle into something, but otherwise the price and messiness are both far too prohibitive (and I got them on sale).  I've bumped it up from two stars to three, however, after considering how they keep the enzymes intact and don't add sulfites.
this does taste like the restaurant version BUT it is very weak so let it seep a long time and/or combo 2 bags to get the true flavor out!

The concept is a good one. Stuff a treat into a rubber toy, and let the dog figure out how to get to the prize. Should keep Fido busy for hours unless like our dogs he loses patience and gives up. After having to remove the Ziggies ourselves most of the time, we've given up and now give the remaining Ziggies to one of our dogs as a snack.

Good: Made in the USA. Piper likes them. Doesn't make our dogs sick. Soft enough for a dog with four missing teeth like our Piper. NO meat-by-products

Not so good: First two ingredients are ground wheat and gelatinized wheat starch. However, there is chicken meal in there too.

Finally - As a treat choice this isn't bad because there are far worse choices out there. As entertainment paired with a Kong, it hasn't worked too well for us. It might work for you.
Great product, but you can get it for $2.50-$3.00 per box at your local grocery store on sale!

I'm not sure it is as decaffeinated as they pretend and it is kind of a regular black coffee with nothing special or particular flavor.
I got a 12 ounce can this week for $1.99 at Safeway. I guess that was a good rebate.

Overall, I'm not impressed.

I have two cats and both of them were a little overweight. I fed them science diet 'light' for quite a while before the 'indoor' came out. Does not seem to be much difference between the 'light' and 'indoor' except for 'indoor' is a little more expensive (same price but less food).

The claimed hairball control does not seem to work. My mid-hair cat still occasionally has hairball problem and I have to give him other stuff to ease that. Nutrition wise, I don't know. I did not switch back to the 'light' just because its name (for indoor cat), but I think essentially they are the same thing.

I find that your lids are good. but they leek causing water to fall on counter. Which is still liveable if you hold the cup up. But my biggest promblem is your shipping for light weight plastic Its almost the same price as the lids. What gives with that.

Fluffy, it isn't, but the loaf rises and keeps well, tastes 'fair-to-middling'. It makes quite a decent sandwich compared to any recipe I have tried in the past 11 years - and believe me, I have tried a LOT of recipes...  I just think it is  pretty pricey, not cheap, but cheaper than buying all those different GF flours, only to turn out a pathetic, crumbly & peculiar-tasting loaf.  So far, this is the best alternative I have found.

The canned version is better (for everything) as it is thicker and tastier.  The bottle version seems to be looser and not as flavorful.  It is admittedly more convenient, but I don't think the loss of flavor is worth the convenience.
Not a good a Sweet-n-low candy but is much better for your teeth. Orange and yellow flavors are the best tasting

I bought these seeds, and they did not grow. However, I think that was me and not the seeds. The weather was really hot and after reading tips, I put them in the wrong soil. However, the company that sent the seeds has a really good website about tips about how to plant the seeds and even offers replacement seeds. I have not contacted them yet, but I plan too.
Loved the first shipment, big flavorful cherries very sweet and slightly tart. Second shipment cherries were considerably smaller, much drier and not nearly as much flavor.

My German Shepherd puppy has never had solid stool since switching him over to premium kibble.  The breeder had him on Science Diet which I've read is not a very good food.  I tried putting him on Blue Buffalo LBP but could never get consistently firm poops.  After reading the reviews I decided to give this brand a try.  Since switching, my pup has consistently good stool in the morning and afternoon, but for some reason by early evening, his stool is still soft (although not a runny as when he was on Blue Buffalo).  The reason I'm giving this a 3 star is that 1. This particular blend smells very fishy.  If you don't mind fish breath on your dog then its not a big deal.  2.  The first ingredient is not a protein thus the protein levels are lower than other premium dog foods.  This may be OK for an adult dog, but I'm not so sure if this is enough for a growing pup.  Which leads me to #3.  You need to feed almost twice the amount of food for growing puppies (probably to make up for the lower levels of protein).  In the end you are actually paying more since the serving size is larger for puppies; also larger serving size means more poop to scoop!  My dog is 8 months old so I might just weather out the next few months on this brand until his growth slows down then try to switch to Taste of the Wild.  I most definitely will not be getting the fish blend again, its too stinky. I may try the bison mix next.

Taste fine. Easy to digest during workouts. My big complaint is that they are thin and crumbly. How do you carry these with you during your workouts? If I put it in my pocket, it crumbles into pieces and is real hard to eat. I much prefer Honey Stinger energy bars because they don't fall apart before I can eat them.

Also the price is kind of expensive. 250 calorie Clif bars cost about a dollar each at my local supermarket. These waffles only have 160 calories for a dollar, so you wind up paying a lot more for the same amount of energy intake (assuming you're trying to eat the same number of calories per hour during your workouts).

This has a slightly sweet, chipotle spice type of flavor, nothing like what I expected. I thought it would taste just like the sauce they use on their tacos but its not. It really didn't add much to the flavor of my taco, it more distracted from the real taco flavors. I didn't care for it but my kids did put it on their tacos and not complain, hence the 3 stars. For me it was just extra calories as it did absolutely nothing for my taco, except make it more creamy.

The first time I tried this, it was not quite chilled enough. Tasted bland with grassy, musty tones and almost a turpentine finish. Chilled properly, it is a bit better. More acid crispiness comes through and light fruity flavors are added. But I found it shows best against lightly sweet foods: fresh blueberries, salads with acidic, lightly sweet dressings, etc. Other pairings were not as good: most fail to bring much notable flavor. I got my money's worth, but not much more.

As we all know.....any canned soup, organic or not, should be avoided or at least limited. It does work for storm supplies due to its easy medium term storage and it being infrequently or never used. It will end up in a hunting camp for a few days of quick meals toward the end of its shelf life. Everything tastes better in fresh air and this stuff isn't bad. Again, its use is very limited.

Don't like the BPA issue either. I did speak to Wolfgang Puck about PBA and their plans. Like most, they are treading water to see what the government (friends of the fda) does or does not do about it. What's a little more poison added to the current mix in processed foods.

Ever notice that most of the Wolfgang Puck soup ingredients here on Amazon end at "Contains 2% or less of the Following"........?

As I indicated above, we did try this soup, and it tasted ok, nothing special. Try adding a little more sea salt. It is better than the MSG enhanced, preservative laden Campbell's brand crap, a brand we would not buy regardless of circumstance. One never knows who actually made this soup.

We consider the organic versions the lesser of (insert remaining cliche), and have a case......in case.

Illy Issimo Cappuccino is a new drnk for me; a brand name I had not tried until recently but one I was anxious to sample. I like cappuccino beverages and I am a regular consumer of coffee, so this beverage sounded like something suitable to my tastes.

This cappuccino drink is a little different from what I expected. Poured from the can into a glass, it looks like chilled hot chocolate with a mocha scent. It also contains a little less volume than I would prefer. The can is only 8.45 fluid ounces in size, so it is consumed completely in a very short time.

As for the taste, it isn't as rich as I was expecting. I wanted something a little stronger and fuller bodied- something closer to an espresso. The taste of this drink, while certainly not bad, isn't very strong. It is chocolaty and coffee- like, as expected, with a creamy, medium to light body. It tends toward the sweet side, which is also not my preference. I drink all coffee- related beverages black, so I am not used to tasting sugar with my roasted brew. In addition, the sugar flavor in this beverage is different in taste and part of the reason is because the manufacturer uses beet sugar. This is probably healthier than refined sugar, but it does result in a little different flavor that may not suit the preferences of different drinkers.

I like a good cappuccino and this one is really not a bad selection. A few tweaks of the recipe would make it a little better, but I agree that it is very easy drinking and has enough good taste to recommend.

These treats are good fun for my dog for about 30 min.  He loves them but it takes about 30 seconds for him to remove the treat from the holder and maybe 15 to 30 minutes to eat the treat.  They are good, I just wish they lasted longer.
I love this product but many of the patties arrived squished and leaky.  Maybe they were place too close to some heat source.  I have ordered the patties before without any problem, however.

I purchased one bag of this at a specialty store.  I made it but added a can of tomato sauce with the hamburger, seasoning and macaroni.  This last time I decided to make it as the bag stated and my family wouldn't eat it.  The tomato sauce helped to mellow it out a bit.  Since I have 5 more bags I will be doctoring it to find the best method of cooking it.  I love Namaste baked goods but this item isn't that great.

Pros:
The popcorn itself is good. My kids and I love popcorn so we like trying different varieties.
Able to mix different types together in the same batch for contrasting flavors and texture.
Works very well in an oil popper. Not a lot of leftover unpopped seeds.

Cons:
Paying something like $10 for shipping. It's likely you can find something very similar to this in a local store (I got a similar 3-pack at Target last year) for a similar price, and will save on the shipping.

Overall, it's good. It's just not a good value because of the shipping costs.
The product is good but one three of the bags were some how opened and got the mix everywhere once we open the box. Good product though....

I gave this 3 stars because a rating is required, and not having purchased it, I am neutral. I would like to know if this comes in beef, chicken, or turkey flavors. I didn't know where toask a ques., so I am postingit in this review section. It looks really good, even for people, even though it is not for people. I hope the packaging issue gets cleared up because I don't like getting cat food juice on me either! Thank you for letting me ask here, and for any help anyone can give me! You're the cat's meow! lol! :)

The cans are tiny, and filled mostly with water, so be very, very careful upon opening. The force needed to bend the lid up is just enough to send the "chicken pot pie" concoction spraying onto everything in vicinity, leaving a puddle with some carrots in it for your cat.
My cat doesn't much care for the carrots. Or for the lumps of wheat glutenish chickenfood, 3-5 per can. This is more of a soup course, or an after-supper tea. Seriously, this barely passes for food, and in no way requires so much packaging.

The sesame chicken, however, has earned a spot on my cat's, and on all of his outdoor pal's, favorites list. The sauce is just viscous enough for genteel lapping, and the julienned meat a considerable presence. Plus: no carrots. This cat food's presentation qualities place it right up in my own top three: if you ever indulge the pre-dawn-feeding cry, you may grow to love this stuff too. Feeding can be done half-asleep and one-handed: give the can a shake, pop the top off, and upend it into a tiny cat bowl.That's it. The interior walls of the can are very smooth -- they may be plastic coated, so check your recycling outfit's guidelines and then discount my next point -- so smooth that the gooey stuff pours right out. No rinsing needed. The odor is quite inoffensive. But if your cat begs to eat it outside, watch out: if the neighborcats smell it, there's gonna be a rumble.

At $4/pack retail, or $1 for three weensy ounces of liquid-plus-some-bits, I canot recommend the signture chicken pot pie. If the brand ever markets the sesame chicken solo, however, and promotional discounts are offered, I'd definitely stock up.

I recently bought Wonka Laffy Taffy Stretchy & Tangy Variety Box, 24-Count, 1.5-Ounce Boxes from Sam's Club and LOVED it. I love the cherry the most, so when I saw this item--ALL CHERRY!--I was excited. The picture on the container didn't say Stretchy & Tangy but the Product Features did...so I thought I was set. Except it's not the Stretchy & Tangy variety...it's just the plain cherry which tastes completely different and was NOT what I was expecting. I'm keeping it since I still like the taffy (and so does my husband) but it's not what I wanted.

I like the flavor of this on popcorn. Using in other foods it is very mild. I wanted something that would give a punch of cheddar flavor to a dish. Not bad but I might try some of the others on the market and see if they are the same, better or worse.
A bit bland, but good in a pinch when I am too tired to cook

Chips are good, but Amazon ships them in their original "ready to ship" box, which turns out is not really so ready for shipping. The box arrived in tatters; miraculously, the chips survived relatively intact. Hopefully will continue to be so lucky in the future.

I liked it but I think it is very similar to Outrageous Ginger Ale except Outrageous Ginger Ale is better. This product was crisp etc. I am sorry I could not give better reviews. My favorite ginger ale is Healthy Valley's ginger ale.

They call it Peppermint Tea and that's exactly what it is! Boy, do you get Peppermint! In fact, even at the 11.5 oz setting of my B70 it's over-powering! I think it would be wonderful on cool winter evenings. But I must admit that I actually had to resort to a little cream to smooth it down.

If you love Peppermint, this is the tea for you!

These bars are slightly dry in my opinion. My sister raves about these bars, so I gave my entire order to her.  I prefer my bars more moist and soft, these are almost crunchy but the taste is very good for 90 calories!

The candy bar itself is one of my favorites. Has all the items that I would want in a bar except I would prefer dark chocolate to the milk chocolate.

The packing was bad. It came with bottle of lotion. One end of the box was mashed making bars on the end mashed together. The lotion had leaked out an inch of lotion making a sticky mess. I didn't report it but was surprised this happened. A first for any item I ordered from amazon.

This espresso tea is wonderfully aromatic, reminds me of cherry tobacco, but does not transfer well to the palate, or at least mine.  The scent is very strong as you are sipping the tea, and it overwhelms me, but I have a keen sense of smell so that may not be a problem for others.  It is hard to differentiate the actual taste from the scent.  I don't think I will try it again.

I have been using Equal and more recently Splenda, as my sweeteners of choice for many years. We use it in coffee, tea and on cereals primarily. My doctor suggested getting away from those artificial sweetners and suggested we try Stevia instead. We did, and as others have suggested.....it does taste different! Not sure I would call it an after taste, but different none the less. It is not a bad taste necessarily, but just differnt. The effect differs based on what you use it for. My suggestion would to be to try a small order first to see how you like it, and whether you can live with the change in taste.

Addendum Januray 2012: I am no longer using the Stevia for my coffee or tea. However, I find that I do not notice the after taste when used on solid foods like my oatmeal or breakfast cereal. FYI, I find that I need to use three packets of Stevia to obtain the same sweetness of two packets of Splenda. Also, because this is a fine powder rather than granules, it is more difficult to use. The packets are made of a sturdy paper product and it is difficult to open it without losing some of the powdery sweetener on your hand, the countertop or in the air.
This salt has a clean flavor and adds nice salinity to dishes.  The crystals are quite large (too large for sprinkling) and a salt grinder is recommended.

These artichoke "hearts" contain too much leaf for my taste.  To be fair, most (NOT all) of the leaf is edible, but these are being sold as hearts.  Still, pretty good artichoke parts if you buy them when the price is right.

Compared to Celestial Seasonings English Breakfast, this tea is weak.  The tea tastes like the second run of the other brand.  Purchased Twinings because much cheaper than C.S., but will not make that mistake again!

Can't tell if I'm really satisfied with these or not.  First, they're hard.  Almost like hard candy.  I tend to mix it with my cereal hoping that they'll soften from the milk but they don't always do.  I'm not sure if you can really benefit from these.  They're so dried that they seem "lifeless" as in the majority of goji benefits have been sucked out.  I won't be buying these again unless I see improvement from eating the rest of these hard goji berries.
very delicious olives, but i think there is too much salt and water added

i am a fan of this coffee, and have bought it many times before in the starbucks stores. i thought this was a good deal buying it through amazon, until i realized that these are NOT the same size bags that starbucks sells!

so just be aware -- these are only 12 OUNCE bags!!!

(no complaint on the coffee itself though)

I love the Soda Stream unit, but the syrups need some tweaks.  It is too sweet, so I use half the amount required; this is good if you want the product to last longer; this is bad because they use Splenda added to all their recipes, not just the diet.  If they would just use plain old sugar, I'd be much happier with this product.

I started taking this when my baby was about 10 months.  I have been trying to make it to one year nursing.  I didn't see a great increase, maybe a little.  It certainly didn't hurt anything to try it.  I have now stopped taking it and didn't see any difference when I stopped either.  I think it's something to try if you are really wanting to continue nursing and see a decrease in your production.

I bought this product because it appears that the teabag version of the Pixie mate chai (all of Pixie's teas actually) are no longer being made or sold and it was my favorite drink. I do not particularly like things that are extremely sweetened so it has been difficult to find the right balance with this concentrate. It is not bad, it is not great either. It is extremely sweet as it has the sugar already in it. The directions recommend mixing half concentrate with half milk and heating. I found this to be overwhelmingly sweet and thick so I use 1/3 concentrate 2/3 almond milk (which is less sweet even than milk) and sometimes dilute with water a bit as well. Note this does NOT taste good diluted with just water.

If you like things that are very sweet you will love this. If you find where they are still selling the teabag version please post!

A little on the acrid side of bitter, but what else could you expect when you order a coffee named "Jet Fuel"?
Definitely one of the best bang for your buck coffees available for the Keurig machines here on Amazon.com. I also loved the no hassle packaging, no extra stuff that will take up room in my recycling bin.
I'd buy it again, but I will have to resupply my vanilla creamer stash waaaay more often. I usually like my coffee black but this one is a bit much! If you love super bold coffee, go for it! If you are a breakfast blend with cream and sugar kinda person, maybe opt for the Donut Shop K-Cups instead.
all 6 caps were loose..A little flat but not too bad, i would try it again but please tighten those caps are trying to kill us...

Switched my non-diabetic (I have one diabetic on wet only for the past year) cat from EVO to Wellness Complete (blue bag) in an attempt to save $ while still providing good nutrition for the fur baby. Ever since starting the Wellness food his litter box has had the most foul odor I have ever smelled in a litter box. Visitors can definitely tell I have pets!! Heck, they probably think I'm secretly hoarding zoo animals. This hasn't been a problem before and I had really been hoping this was a temporary thing but we're almost three months into a bag and there's been no let up. We're finally getting to the last of the bag and I'm going to start switching him back to the EVO because I literally can't take it anymore. I'm quite frankly shocked that no one else has complained about this.

To summarize:

PROs:
Pretty solid nutrition
Cat seems to really like the taste
Cheaper than other holistic brands

CONs:
Twice a day it smells like raw sewage all through-out my house. No thanks!

Since it's practically impossible to find good yakisoba short of flying to an area with an actual Japantown, I bought these to see if it would be a suitable alternative however I am somewhat disappointed. The texture is indeed better than the cheap 25cent Maruchan cup ramen noodles at your local supermarket and the fact that it comes with some cabbage and toppings is a plus. However, the taste has been "Americanized" to the point where you really can't tell that these noodles are supposed to be yakisoba. The chicken flavoring packet is similar to the one that you would find in most other chicken cup ramen so I wasn't overly thrilled with it.

If you don't absolutely need "instant" noodles, you can save money by just going to Costco and purchasing the Top Ramen (the ones that you need to boil) and minimize the amount of water used to boil the noodles (so as to get a "drier" noodle). The taste and texture is comparable to these Maruchan yakisoba bowls.

If you want a more accurate yakisoba taste, I would instead try the Myojo Ippeichan Yakisoba Japanese Style Instant Noodles, 4.77-Ounce Tubs (Pack of 6). They tend to cost a little more per bowl but the taste and texture is more authentic and you do get some vegetable toppings as well.

The grape leaves are tougher than expected. Those of us with false teeth would be had pressed to bite through them. There is no refrigerate after opening warning on the lable nor is there a use before date.
