I bought this for a skinned knee that wouldn't heal. I read a little about this honey before I ordered it and thought more powerful is better. I did more research and clinical studies from New Zealand have proven that MGO 250 (old 16+) is just as effective at less than half the price.

The reason that Manuka honey works is probably due to its methylglyoxal content (which is a common element in many foods). Unfortunatley, methylglyoxal is considered to be a genotoxin. I use it externally but I'm a little reluctant to consume it regularly. It does help wounds heal without infection. I put a little on the wound and cover it with a adhesive bandage or gauze. The bandage needs to be changed regularly.

It does work as an antacid. It takes about a teaspoon -- preferably on a small pice of bread.

I live on a mountain side with 20 acres heavily populated by squirrels. We have the big gray and flying that love our attic. I bought the sonic sounders and put ammonia in the attic with little to no success. A handyman gave me a bottle of this to spray on the rodents entry points and PRESTO those guys are gone! If I don't reapply every three weeks or so they return but then a couple sprays in there entry point and gone again!

This stuff is a little pricey but a good night sleep is priceless.

Appian Way pizza is a family tradition in our house. My mother in law introduced us to it. The crust is not what sets this pizza mix apart it's the sauce! The sauce is amazing! In order to get the pizza to stretch out nicely and be much easier to work with use 2 boxes. It makes a heartier pizza that stretches to any cookie sheet! Another trick is to make the dough as directed using two boxes, then soak a dish towel in hot water. Wring the towel out until its damp. Set on top of the bowl and place in the oven for at least an hour. The dough will fit on a large cookie sheet and stretch nicely.

This coffee allows for a nice cup of java and seems to get a bit more crema than my old brand. It has a rich flavor, but not as bold as I hoped it would be. The price is good and delivery was fast using Amazon. Don't be afraid to use a bit more than normal, and tamp it well. As always, hot milk is the way to go . . . 2% is fine.
This is a fairly decent soup but the shrimp were pretty tiny and broken up. If they improved that it would be much better. Nice tasting however.Glad I got it on sale here.

For anyone who remembers those fudgy little cookies and has been missing them, this is a good news/bad news story. The bad news--the crisp cookie part of this treat is a chocolate one, unlike the plain vanilla of Fudge Patties past. The good news--you probably won't notice the difference.

For the uninitiated: this is a lighter, more crisp version of a vanilla wafer (though chocolate), slightly hollowed out to accommodate a dollop of creamy fudge. The whole thing is then covered in more chocolate.

This is no gourmet cookie; but for chocolate lovers who've never forgotten the joy of biting into that thick, creamy fudge layer before finding the crunchy cookie inside, it's not bad.

Serving suggestion: Best eaten at warm-ish room temp, when the outer blanket of chocolate is just soft enough to be a bit tacky but not messy, allowing your teeth to sink into the inner fudgy layer...with a glass of milk nearby.

I have tried early artificial sweeteners but they left a bad after taste. Splenda sweetens just great and no after taste. The packets are very handy and not that expensive. And I like the "sweet" sayings on each packet!

Don Maffitt

Just like everyone else here it seems, I first experienced Haribo's magic in Germany. I was at a train station and I needed a quick snack, so I bought a little bag of the Gold-Bears. Ever since I ventured to find them in the States, but couldn't. A few years ago, however, I noticed them popping up in their little bags, and had to buy one.
While they're still the best gummy bears Stateside, I was a bit disappointed since they were harder than I had them in Deutschland. But that's understandable, as I'm assuming they're imported from Germany, and gummy bears really can't retain their freshness for long when traveling across the sea, and then sitting on a store shelf waiting for someone to buy them. They're not hard-hard like some of the other gummy bear brands you'll find here; they're just harder than in Europe.

The flavors are strong and fantastic, and I have to stop from eating so many gummies at once for fear of my jaw getting sore--but they're so good!

The 5lb bag is a great deal, but just be sure no one else is around. I already had a bunch of co-workers coming up to get some, assuming they'll last forever since it's a large bag. After ordering this about 2 weeks ago, I'm already having to consider reordering a second bag!

We tried this product for our son who is 7 and gluten intolerant. It really is quick and easy to prepare. The servings are individually measured and comes with a measuring cup for adding water. The bread results are not really a whole lot like traditional sandwich bread. The single serve slices turned out with consistency more along the lines of a pancake and seemed a bit thicker than a regular slice of white bread. With that said, they worked out just fine for making PB&J and my son had no complaints about the taste. (I didn't try the bread myself so can't comment on the taste personally).
I recommend trying this out for yourself if you haven't found happiness with any other GF breads.

Sweet potatoes are among my favorite vegetables, and I especially adore sweet potato chips. So an Amazon Vine offer of these chips seemed a sure bet.

They taste a bit like sweet potatoes, yet ever so slightly sweeter --- with fewer calories and half the fat of a bag of real sweet potato chips (100 calories, 30% from fat, compared to 130 calories with half from fat in a regular bag of chips).

But I agree with others. The taste is slightly strange --- and the ingredients tell why. The key ingredient isn't sweet potato, but RICE FLOUR! Sweet potato flakes (whatever those are) come second, then tapioca starch. Next comes oil (sunflower, safflower, or canola) then yellow corn flour. And finally there's cane syrup --- sugar --- which explains why the chips seem a tad sweeter than sweet potatoes.

I like these Sweet Potato Popchips well enough, and will keep the box at the ready for brown bag lunches over the next several weeks.

I may buy them again, too --- but only if no real sweet potato chips are available to satisfy my sweet potato tooth.

Just as I would expect form a sipping chocolate, this came out chocolatey without the extra sugariness. I really liked it. The poweder is super fine, which can be a pain to work with when you're trying not to make a mess. The end result is tasty tho - just stir thoroughly.

I recommend following the 4 oz. directions for a rich, velvetey drink. I even tried this with soy! Would buy again, but wish it was less pricey.

My mom loves these things. She eats them by the handful during Easter. Nice to be able to get them online in a large quantity and have them delivered for free, but we found them somewhere else for half the price with free (but slower) shipping.

Yum!

These noodles are tasty, my family and I like them. I add sauteed vegetables and tofu for a full meal. The taste is spicy but we like it that way. The citrus flavor is better than the peanut which is too bland I think. I'll reorder it when we are out...

The beads provide a nice tingly texture to the lather and it has a nice smell, which isn't too overpowering. I don't care for it as a face wash, but for a body wash it does what it advertises. The smell isn't too feminine or overpowering, it lathers up well, and does a good job of cleaning without leaving a residue or film. Four stars because it doesn't work for us well as a face wash, but does a good job of cleaning other bits.
Tastey and straong for a bag tea. It really works as a sleep aid. It does have ingredents that may aggravate sensitive people.
Good for my need plus it's says me the guess work. Taste good too!! it came to my door so fast it made me have movie night in the middle of the week

I've been using sweetleaf for 5 years now.  I love this product, especially the zero glycemic index which all stevia does not have.  The only complaint I would ever have is that the powder form doesn't dissolve well in cold drinks.  You should use the liquid form for this.

There is almost a misnomer in the title of this product. It is not a Latte; rather, it is more of a peppermint cocoa flavored beverage. Still very good and has the hints of Christmas you would expect from something like this product. A nice clean aftertaste and refreshing for a hot beverage. Give it a try.

The Coffeemate Liquid little cups...........are great BUT
the powder is the best.........good deal for sure, next time,
it's the powder! Note to brain! LOL

Authentic Smokey Mountain origins.....uh no.

However, this thick rich habanero elixir has an "instant on" smack you in the face heat factor,
and it should cause there's nothing in here except peppers, vinegar, and salt. Lovely!

The heat is bearable and the flavor is terrific. I've never seen anything like it, and it makes many
things from Bloody Marys to burgers to Vienna Sausages much improved. I just love the smoked
flavor.

Now, why the minus one star? These guys are not from the hills of Tennessee or North Carolina, they
are actually up in the Catskills (New York). That ain't exactly what I define as "Appalachian."

These are pretty much the same honey graham crackers from long ago, with that great grainy flavor with a hint of honey. They are in a smaller size. Fine, I never had much of a problem with the original size, but whatever makes us happy. I guess this size will help keep portions wrapped and fresh. I just wish Nabisco would dispense with one old custom: using partially hydrogenated oil(PHVO). Yes, if they do use it, it is a small enough quantity to meet the requirement of being listed as zero grams of trans fats, but it adds up. In this case, this product may or may not contain PHVO. So, it is obvious that PHVO is not absolutely necessary to produce this product, nor is it an economic necessity. So, we should ask ourselves, since we know it isn't good for us(that is why the amount present is listed on the nutritional panel)and is totally artificial, why does Nabisco have to deal with it? Don't they CARE?
Let's keep in mind that the CEO of Nabisco make lots and lots of dough(sorry for the pun), so maybe they should be replaced with someone who can manage to pay attention to producing the best possible product for the best possible price. I would be happy to take the job.
Christmas gift for a movie gift package!  Convenient & fast shipping from Amazon for a something a little extra in a themed gift!

A friend had recommended Rooiobos tea and I searched for one available via K-cups.  This one is delicious!  It's a dark tea that really taste like a dark tea rather than green tea which although I like can sometimes seem like an underbrewed tea.  Fabulous that it is naturally caffeine free too.  Perfect for the late afternoon when I want a cup of tea, but don't want the caffeine.

This Lady Grey loose tea is a sensory experience. It is light and citrusy with just the right kick of caffeine. The flower petals are pretty but I cannot taste any difference they might make in the steeped tea. It would make a nice gift for a woman who you don't know very well. All in all it is worth a try.

Definitely found out that although this flavor is great, it stains anything and everything. Even if I use one tub to four quarts, it's VERY dark. I have decided to stick with the lighter colored Crystal Lights to prevent anything else being red. :)

This is good coffee, easy on the stomach.  The best part is that if you make a really strong pot of coffee, it doesn't taste bitter.  The roasting was first-rate without extra oil left on the beans.  And it's a very good buy for shade-grown, fair-trade coffee.

While the toy is certainly of good quality and seems to hold up thus far. One should be made wary of the possibility of this turning into a deadly weapon in the jaws of the right K-9. I was dealt a crippling blow which brought me to my knees as my pup came and beat the ever living crap out of me with it in excitement and desire for more treats.

Hi ordered to taste different coffees what i did not relize that 25 percent would be decafe. Would like more for four or six instead of two of each type to try.also dont want to try decafe brands for me a waste of time drinking coffee.

Like several products this dandruff shampoo really works.  A difference between most others is that have that clinical smell, while Clear Men Scalp Therapy 2 does not.  As an added bonus, this product also contains conditioner, taking care of your dandruff problem but leaving your hair  clean and fluffy.  If there is one thing I don't like is the container - it's just a better of personal preference but I would prefer a more stable base.

All of Kikkoman instent soups are great.  An easy half cup of warm broth with vegetables and little squares of tofu, this soup warms and comforts without a lot of calaries and fat.  A quick pick-me-up anytime.

i followed pediatrician recommendations to start with rice cereals and oatmeals etc. mixed with breastmilk. they all seem like sawdust, though. so if you're going to be like me and feed your kid sawdust, this is probably the best sawdust there is with all its DHA and organic goodness.
My 9 year old daughter and the entire family Love it!  It really is very tasty and quick & easy to prepare.

I love my morning cup of coffee. I don't care for the heavy sweetness in a Starbuck's Pumpkin Spice Latte; this
is a good match for me. Light and spicey.
Easy way to have a snack on hand that adds protein and curbs those sugar lows.

This is an excellent oil. the only question I still have about it is is it centrifuged expelled oil. It is organic and unrefined and that's good. but reading the label it doesn't inform much of the process of making this oil.
I use the oil to help me with candida issues along with Kefir and it is going extremely well. At first you may get gas but once the candida subsides gas will go away. I use it topically on my whole body and do oil hair treatments as well once a week. Coconut oil is miraculous to say the least, if you need to know more on it get this book: "The coconut oil miracle" by Bruce Fife.

Cuddle up with your favorite book,throw and a cup of this chocolately mint flavored coffee.A refreshing way to relax after a hectic day or a good morning warm up drink to start a cold day.

Cheaper and quicker than you local coffee house.

4.25*rating.
We had these cookies in Victoria, BC; I wanted to get more for gifts from our trip to Canada but forgot about it.  When I got home Amazon had them and I was able to give them as gifts as planned.
Tea is great and works well in the Senseo.  Flavor is good and strong.  Only complaint is th. at it is quite pricey for tea.
Sardines taste fresh, but there is a lot of oil.  I would like the can packed, but there is space for lots of oil.

When I was a kid there used to be a grated American cheese product that was put out by Kraft.  I don't know if it was available everywhere, but it was always at the local A&P in my town, and I came to like it better than any of the fancy grated Parmesan or Romano cheeses.  It came in the very same 3 oz containers like here on Amazon.  Something of a pain for I liked it so much I didn't care how much it cost, I just wanted it all the time. (It would have been nice if it came in larger sizes). There was simply nothing like its flavor on pasta.  It was easily distinguishable by its yellow/orange color, and its much tangier, richer cheese taste.  My father, along with many others considered it junk compared to grated Parmesans, but I didn't really care what was in it.  I only knew it gave pasta a whole new flavor that was as deliciously cheesy in a grated form that was available.  A long time ago it disappeared from many local stores.  My father used to tell me that they stopped making it because only two people would buy it.  Me, and the guy that invented the stuff.  But according to the reviews here I see I am not alone.  This product is essentially the same thing as the grated american cheese of my youth in the very same small 3 oz containers.  And I am happy to report that it is just as fabulously delicious as I remember it.  Ordering 12 at once will not see it go bad here.  We have spaghetti at least once in a week in my house and I load it with this stuff.  I am a self confessed grated cheese fiend, but nothing compares to this  topping in my opinion.  It's not pure, it's not really healthy, it's not aged all that much, it's just plain delicious.  It can  be compared to chomping down a hot dog smothered with mustard and ketchup and enjoying it immensely, and someone telling you there is no real food in it, or good for you. You don't eat hot dogs everyday, and you won't eat this that often either.  If you like grated cheese like I do, I would strongly urge you to try this grated american cheese product.  Its the most flavorful grated cheese topping around, and I recommend it.  My only reason for taking one star off is the price.  With shipping its a little pricey, but still worth every cent.  It's really hard to find in stores, and even when you do they tend to run out.  It seems to be always here on Amazon, and I say give it a delicious try....

A very enjoyable breakfast cereal, sweetened but not cloyingly so. Could be crunchier (it's nowhere near as crunchy as Wheat Chex, the gold standard of crunchiness in my book). The box didn't last long around our house!
They taste great. But the package was pretty poorly put together and half of the beans tins were beat up.

couldn't be happier with the price. I've got it in my bulk freezer to keep it fresh and fill up a tupper ware full of tea once a month. probably a half an once or once a month at most. really good tea for the price.

It's very difficult to find healthy prepared foods that are low in salt. Dr. Joel Fuhrman's line of canned food is a wonderful find for me. I wish it was organic, so I lop off a star for that, but I haven't been able to find anything else like this out there, organic or not. Most "low salt" foods are really still pretty high in salt, but Vitabeanavegamin is an exception, with only 110mg of salt in the entire can (4% of USRDA). It takes a little while to get used to low salt foods, because we're all so used to having salt in everything (especially soup!), but it's true that if you give your taste buds a few days to adjust, you'll start to find "normally" salted foods way too salty, and the flavor of the truly low salt foods just pops right out.
Nutritionally, this soup is great. To be honest, I don't eat it as a soup but rather as it comes out of the can, which is very dense (even denser than a stew). The whole can is 280 calories, with a total of 110mg of salt, 1g of fat, 980% of daily requirements for vitamin A, 70% of vitamin C, and 20% each of calcium and iron. Even better, there's 14g of fiber (58% USRDA) and 14g of protein. After I eat a can, I actually feel "energized".
Also very good are Dr. Fuhrman's Supreme Greens and Dr. Fuhrman's Moroccan Chick Peas.

This stuff is really f'n good. The only downside of this is the digusting intestine tube package. One of the upsides of synthetic animal chunks is that you don't have to package them in synthetic animal pieces. I would buy this a lot more often if it came in a little tub.

Sipping a cup of tea while I write this review on a rainy day...ahh. Good times!

Pros: the tea bags. The pyramid bag is the greatest invention Lipton could have done for their teas. Easy to bob in and out of the water, quick to steep and nice to leave in the water, strong enough to go back for refill without the tea tasting too watered down. The best? Mix a little bit of agave or stevia and it takes the drink to the next level!

Pro: Good even as ice tea. Does take two bags for a gallon of tea, but I actually liked it a little bit better as an ice tea than a hot tea.

Con: I wanted the taste to be stronger on the vanilla side. It didn't have the smooth taste I was expecting and associated with vanilla. It tasted very much like an herb tea, which isn't a bad thing, I just wanted the stronger combination.

Con: the tea bag only lasts about one cup of tea. I was used to Lipton having a reputation to last forever and 'ever. But let it sit in a dish over night, there is no tea left for another cup. It's a one and done, kind of tea.

Overall, I did like it. Good flavor, great packaging (again, love that bag!), it just didn't have the power of flavor I had hoped for.

I have tried many foods with my dog's sensitive stomach. I have limited his treats and human food but he still ends up sick. I have been working with natural foods and non-preservative foods and they seem to be better.  I found this brand at a local store and he rarely has issues anymore.  I am so happy with this product.  However, it is hard to find, at this time.  If your dog has food allergies or other food issues like mine, you really need to try this.
Satisfyingly sweet with lots of protien. I eat it as dessert or quick pick me up.

I tried the watermelon strawberry and the black cherry switch and of the two, I'd go with the black cherry every time. The watermelon strawberry was ok, but it didn't have the burst of flavor I expected. Still, this is far better than drinking soda pop and the cans are about the size of a Red Bull can.

If you like watermelon and strawberry, you might enjoy this. I found it was good, but not as good as some of the other Switch drinks I've tried.

This is very easy to mix up, and the taste is plain pizza dough. Have some gluten-free flour of some sort on hand (or use some extra of this mix), this is a very sticky dough starting out. I'd recommend a liberal brushing with some garlic olive oil before adding toppings (just mince some garlic and mix it into a cup of olive oil), otherwise the crust can get pretty hard on the edges.

For someone who loves pizza, but can't have wheat or gluten, this is the best thing out there.

EDIT: We've since discovered the Chebe products, which are much more like bread. The pizza crust is excellent, not sticky like Orgran and available on Amazon.

I'd ask our English Setters, Toby and Abby, to rate these treats, but they won't work for free and Deb already has them plumped up beyond "fluffy." Actually, Toby is somewhat less enthused than Abby, which is OK with her, because as soon as Toby turns his back, she eats his as well - and begs for more. You snooze, you lose. The only quibble I have is with the price - we don't pay this much per pound for our own food. On the other hand, if they only cost $3 or $4, I'd have to buy a crate full every month. The best I've been able to do so far is swear I'll never pay this much again, wait two weeks and order another couple of bags. Believe Abby would rate them 10 stars if she could type. These treats are generally a little less expensive that the competition (and I think equally good, although I confess I've not actually eaten any myself), so they are usually ordered more often.

I am really picky about snack bars. I was anxious to try this one especially since its gluten-free. The bars are really good. They don't have that weird chemically sweet taste that some bars do. I think this is from the short list of ingredients.
The only reason I didn't give these 5 stars is that some times they are a little hard. It varies from just the right consistency to "I am glad I have strong teeth" but the taste is consistent and always excellent.

3 dogs, 1 loves it and uses it as intended. The only complaint there is that he's become far too good at it and learned how to push the rope in and out very quickly. He 48 lbs, gets his regular meals in it and finishes in about 15 minutes. I wish it took him longer but it sure is awesome watching him be so good at it! Worked great for the second dog for a few weeks, he wasn't as good at it, so it took him a bit longer to empty it so we thought it might be perfect for him. We were wrong, he chewed the rope in half one day. :-( Third dog is just kind of dumb and just smells it and looks at it. The plastic is really rugged though, they're able to toss it around on stained concrete floors without breaking it!

Overall, I LOVE this company's toys. One of my dogs chewed a Kong but hasn't been able to destroy Premier's Squirrel toy. Dumb dog likes the Twist 'n' Treat, it doesn't take very much brain power...

The peach mango flavor is tasty.  It is a good balance of sweet and tangy.  A nice need addition to the Kool Aid flavor options.  Generally a user of sugar free options, I go this one for my son to use in his magic slushy maker which works better with sugar-based juices.  I tried this one out and liked the flavor enough that I hope it comes out in a sugar-free variety.
I buy the vegetable juice for my son so that he can take it to school which can give him some vitamin and fibres.

My vegetarian wife has used Morga Vegetable Broth for years. But suddenly it disappeared and no easily accessible shop seems to carry it anymore.  Your product item, Seitenbacher, seemed to be similar and we were hoping better - however, we're Morga nuts, and pretty hard to satisfy!
Was looking for a brand other than sense and came across Baronet, could not be more pleased.  Great flavor, rich and tasty each and every time.  Will reorder again that is for sure.

I'm glad I read the reviews saying to only use a few drops in a beverage. Too many drops and it quickly goes from delicious to strange and bitter. The directions on the bottle say 5-8 drops, but I find 2 or 3 is perfect in a 12 oz drink or a cup of yogurt.

I've gotten this sampler twice now and I love it. One of the reasons why I love my Keurig is the variety it brings me. I don't have to be tied down to one bag of one flavor of coffee. Maybe this morning I need an extra-bold, because I hate mornings. Or maybe I want to sip something light and flavorful all afternoon.

I think this sampler does an excellent job of variety. There's regular coffees and flavored ones, light, medium and extra-bold. There are occasionally a few repeats, but that's bound to happen and I don't hold it against them. There is also a good representation of many of the brands as well. Van Houtte, Gloria Jean, Green Mountain, Wolfgang Puck and Donut House coffees are the ones that spring immediately to mind. It's also really good if you're new to owning a Keurig and want to know what kind of coffees are out there and finding which ones you like. (And don't like; in any variety pack, there's going to be some flavors you don't agree with.)

Yes, this does come in a brown paper sack. It's maybe not the classiest-looking thing, but I'm not here for the aesthetics, I just want some coffee.

This straightforward side has rich, bold flavor, with firm cubed paneer (pressed cottage cheese) in thick gravy. The taste grabs and holds your attention so that, though it's a side dish, it doesn't cower meekly by the entrée. Though this is a vegetarian (not vegan) dish, the intense gravy gives the firm paneer a beef-like texture and flavor. It stands well beside any Indian, and many Western, main dishes.

One simple warning: this dish produces plenty of gravy, but far less paneer than the package photo suggests. You should serve this dish with rice, bread, or another simple starch to absorb the excess; otherwise, you'll have a plate of gravy and nothing to eat with it. I find it mixes well with basmati rice, though I imagine it would also blend with onion kulcha or other Indian bread.

I've been trying to make roasted chickpeas for years and never had much success. They were always burned or chewy. So, I was super-excited to see this new product! I got the sampler so I could try all four flavors. I thought the sea salt and chile & lime flavors were pretty gross. The cracked pepper, however, isn't bad and the sweet cinnamon is FANTASTIC. I'll definitely be buying more of that flavor. And for the reviewers who complained about the dryness... they're dried beans, what exactly were you expecting? :-)

This shampoo is fine. I don't have anything bad to say about it. I normally use salon shampoos for color treated hair but would definitely use this if I was in a pinch and needed to pick something up at the store to use.

If you use natural peanut butter, then this mixer is a must have! Initially, it takes awhile to get the peanut butter mixed but if you use it often it doesn't take as long in subsequent uses. The mixer definately cuts down on the mess of mixing peanut butter. The paddle really does come out clean!

If you're used to that cola from Atlanta or in the red white and blue can from New York, you're probably going to be disappointed with the taste.

But is it an acceptable cola as colas go? Yes. I'd even say as a mixer, it'd be fine. There is a heavy aftertaste of carmelized sugar, and that does impact the taste of the cola itself but it is drinkable even if the folks used to Atlanta's finest despise it. Muddy it up with something like flavored syrup (cherry, vanilla, etc) or Rum and it isn't as noticeable.

Also remember that with cola and other "dark" syrups, you have to increase the level of carbonation. I typically do 4-5 buzzes for the right amount of fizz.

I'd put it above the tea taste of the Natural root beer as it's drinkable but still below the lemon/lime and Ginger Ale Natural flavors.

I bought this because it was offered from the Amazon Warehouse Deals section.  Just know that it arrives in a 2lb bag, not the container as shown in the picture.  There were a lot of broken pieces too, that did not detract from the flavor of course.  I got a good deal and my family likes the treat.  When we run out, if it is offered again I will definitely buy it.

Pros:
- Delicious
- Moist and chewy as advertised
- Gluten- and dairy-free, if you need that

Cons:
- As with all makers of granola-type bars, why insist on individually packing each bar? Isn't there a more environmentally friendly way?

I have always been fond of graham crackers. These are not delicious, and they have a strong oat taste that I found distracting from my ideal graham cracker taste. They also have oats sprinkled on the top of them that are more to remind you that these are oat-based than for any other reason that I can detect. I also have a concept of the size of a graham cracker box, and this box looked significantly smaller in comparison.

That being said, I was happy to have this as an option to feed to a young child, for whom high fructose corn syrup and other such ingredients seemed particularly undesirable. They are reasonably tasty (especially for fans of oats) but not fantastic.

My single box of graham crackers was shipped by Amazon in a bubble envelope, and many of my graham crackers were broken, particularly around the edges.

I bought this for my son who is Gluten intolerant and he said it was really good (he's 23).
Apparently regular oatmeal can have traces of Gluten depending on how/where they manufacture it. But this was successfully devoured without any illness. For as many packs as you get, it's probably one of the better deals in the gluten free world....unfortunately.....most all specialty products are pricey.
After trying a lot of different types of food for my puppie (havanese) she has settled on the dried brief Stella and chewy. I just grind it and put some hot water in there and she gulps it all up.

it's nice to know that the juice is organic and not from conventionally grown apples(which has pesticides, junky fertilizers etc.). you really can't tell the difference from this and the regular apple juice, which may be a good thing for my kids. all in all i'm pleased with the purchase.

This Havahart "Critter Ridder" is effective at repelling the animals that make a habit of frequenting my low, rock fence line, most notably squirrels, rabbits, squirrels, and the nasty little dog that the neighbor likes to let do it's "business" in my yard. We don't normally buy the packets of Little Friskies, but since our cats
have been not eating quite as much lately, we wanted to get some packets
of food for less waste than a full can.

Amazon had a great deal on the box of packets, so it was a good time to try them.
(Our local stores do carry them, but I don't get out very often these days.)

So far, both cats like the food. They love the canned Friskies, but wasn't sure if
they'd like the packets. So far so good. Like all packet foods, there is a higher
water content, but while it is a little annoying to essentially be paying for extra
water, it is still good for the puddytats. They can always use more hydration.

The food itself was made with cats in mind, for sure. I say that, because some cat
foods look like they were made for dogs with a flavor adjustment for cats! Honking big
bites, strange bits, etc. The Friskies packets have very nice small bite-sized
bits of food, which both cats seem to enjoy. Even when feeding them Friskies from
the can, there is normally a lot of food on the floor when they are done - they pull
out bigger pieces onto the floor to work on them, or they just get messy. So far,
the Friskies packets are small enough bites that neither cat is pulling the food
out of the dish to eat it.

The only other thing I would say about them is that they seem to have a little less
actual food in them than some other packets we've tried. By that, I mean that splitting
one packet between the cats is normally 1 meal for them both. (They eat a couple times a day.)
With Friskies, it sometimes takes a packet each to satisfy them. Not sure if they just like
the food better (always a possibility), or if there is just a little less than the amount
in some other food packets. By that, I mean food volume, not weight. Water obviously makes
up a higher percentage of the weight in these packets, so looking at the packet weight alone
is not a good indicator of actual food quantity.

Either way, they are happy, the quality seems okay, so that makes us happy.

UPDATE Jan 9, 2012:
We are still buying these, because our cats still love them.
My only real complaint is that Purina is a genius at marketing... in wanting to reduce the
amount of food in each packet without seeming cheap, they added more water to make the weight
similar. Since the water will make gravy no matter what if there is other food in there, they
called it "Gravy Sensations" like it was a well-thought-out plan to make cats happy.
So, you get a lot less food and a lot more gravy in them since the changeover (you have the older
version if you have the black and white cat on the boxes, the new version if you have the ginger
tabby on the boxes).

But, I'll still buy them, but I really watch the price, as I know I am buying
mostly flavored water. However, I have not changed foods, as this is often the only way
to get our girl kitty cat to get enough liquids in her. Just be aware of the high amount
of water in these packets.

By the way - if you run hot water over the packet for a few minutes, it helps to warm up the
food and unstick the pieces of food from the bottom of the packets. It also makes it a little
nicer for the cats (at least I'd like to think so!).

When Kraft parmesan is first opened, the smell somehow makes you feel a slight bite and also makes your mouth water. I strongly recommend that you try to keep this cheese as short a period of time as possible to keep it as fresh as possible. By doing so, you will enjoy Kraft parmesan each time you use it.

I haven't tried this tea yet, but the description is a little misleading.  When it is said that this cake can make 75 servings, what they really mean is that you can have 75 "Gong-fu" sessions with this tea.  This type of Chinese tea is typically put into very small Yixing teapots (approx 5-7gr of tea into a 110-120 ml teapot), rinsed once or twice (probably once for this expensive tea), and then poured into teacups.  A very high-quality Puerh (aged "raw", not aged "cooked") can make anywhere from 5-10 teapots-full of the tea before running out of leaf.  Sometimes even more.  Usually the desired effect of these very-old teas is not exactly how they taste, because often-times they won't taste like much more than flavored water, but instead the "Cha-Chi", which is a type of energy or feeling that your body feels when/after drinking these teas.  The feelings can be anything from quite stimulating, to very soothing (almost narcotic).  There are many fakes in the market-place, due to extremely rare occurences of any REALLY good, old raw Puerh tea being found outside of Asia.  Any that are found will definitely command very high prices because this type of tea is usually hoarded in China, Taiwan, and anywhere else that anyone can find any of it available for purchase.  Also, when someone states "60's Puerh tea", that is a whole decade of variance to deal with.  Before taking the plunge with Puerh tea, start doing your research.  Puerh tea has really been taking hold of the West in recent years, and now the East is capitalizing on our desires for really good Puerh teas.  There are some very good reliable sources out there, but it usually incurs a monetary learning-curve before you get the hang of who you can trust, and what Puerh teas may be right for you.  BUYER BEWARE!  I hope I am not overstepping any bounds by saying this, but a good place to start learning about Puerh tea would be "Puerh Tea- A Westerner's Quest" website.  Good luck, and Good health!

To help eliminate some of the confusion about buying Skinless and Boneless Sardines packed in pure olive oil, I bought the Reese brand in both the 3.75 oz can and the 4.375 oz can and compared them side by side.

Comparison:
3.75 oz Reese Skinless and Boneless Sardines packed in Pure Olive Oil:
The package on the 3.75 oz size stated that the sardines are a product of Morocco. Inside the 3.75 oz can were 3 fairly large sardines. The sardines were packed nicely laying on their sides head to tail, very clean looking, and mostly intact. The flavor was fairly mild but still very good. I was slightly disappointed about the size of these as I tend to like the flavor and texture of smaller sardines.

For this reason, and because of some slight flaking of one of the sardines in the can, I am rating these sardines a "3.7", and rounding this up to a "4" out of "5". I expect that the smaller sardines may hold their form better throughout the canning process.

Comparing the 4.375 oz Reese Skinless and Boneless Sardines packed in Pure Olive Oil:
The package on the 4.375 oz size stated that the sardines are a product of Portugal. The sardines in this can were smaller than those in the 3.75 oz can but were still slightly larger than what I'm used to. There were 4 sardines in the can packed side by side head to tail. They were nearly perfect being fully intact. The flavor and texture was very good. I noticed that there seemed to be a bit more residual moisture in these sardines and also mixed in the olive oil. I can't flaw the sardines for this as some may enjoy the additional moisture which was flavorful and didn't negatively impact the firm texture of these sardines.
Overall I'm rating this 4.375 oz size "4.2" which I'll round down to a "4" out of "5". If this were a 1 - 10 rating system the 4.375 oz can would definitely stand out as a better product. Unfortunately on a 1 - 5 star rating basis it was necessary to rate both cans at "4".

Please Note:
In checking Amazon's current listing for the 4.375 oz can of Reese Skinless and Boneless Sardines packed in Pure Olive Oil, it states that the sardines are a product of Morocco (7/29/10). As stated above the 4.375 size I rated was from Portugal. I've had great sardines from both countries but I'm still learning what's best. After all, looking to the future, who knows what may be found in the waters near either of these places. For now sardines appear to be a very healthy food choice.

The nutritional data on both sizes stated that there were 2 servings per can and the calories stated 110 per serving if drained. So if you eat a full can, it's actually 220 calories if drained.

Interesting that both the 4.375 oz and the 3.75 oz. cans state that there are 2 servings per can when drained. Both state 110 calories per serving even though the cans are quite different in size. If I ever do another comparison, I'll measure the amount of oil and liquid per can versus the amount of solids.

If something sounds too good to be true, it probably is. And cream cheese-ey fruit dips, or marshmallow "fluff" spread, cannot possibly be duplicated without calories. That is a fact of life.

This marshmallow dip should not be compared to either of those foods, both of which are high in calories, sugar, and taste. This dip should be compared to all the other low-calorie sweets out there that don't have potential to derail a diet. And in that field, this dip definitely stands out, both in its taste and in the fact that it packs NO nutritional punch. For me, it's good for a sweet tooth kick during the dog days of a diet. It leaves a major aspartame after-taste, so if that's something you really hate, then don't get this. I personally don't mind.

I think the seriousness of your diet -- and your sensitivity/repulsion to after-tastes from artificial sweeteners -- will determine whether this is a winner for you or not. It is obviously a big jar of chemicals. (Though I'm sure there are plenty of chemicals in other marshmallow dips, too.) For that reason, I wouldn't make this a daily part of my diet any more than I would any other purely artificial food. But it sure is great, again, for the dog days of a diet.

Shake and Bake is really easy to make: simply put the Shake and Bake in a plastic bag, wet your chicken a little and toss in and SHAKE SHAKE SHAKE! Bake it for about 45 minutes at 400 degrees and you'll end up with some crispy "almost like fried" chicken. The flavor isn't too salty, and leans more on the mild side. If you like it a little spicier, rub on a little tabasco before coating the chicken.

This version of Shake and Bake doesn't come with the shaker bag included. You will need to either 1) have a ziploc bag to put the chicken in, or you can just put the S&B in a pie dish (or other shallow dish) and coat it that way. We don't like using too many bags, so we just used a large bowl and tossed the chicken around until coated.

For people who are having problems with getting soggy bottoms on your chicken, an easy way to keep that from happening is to crumple up the foil and put the chicken on top. This creates some air pockets under the chicken so that less of it is sitting on the foil. If you're using chicken wings, you won't even have to crumple the foil because most of the chicken is off the pan. You can also use a wire rack to make the whole chicken crispy. Each pack can coat about 6 pieces (we did 2 each of wings, thighs, and drumsticks and had a little left over in the bowl).

First, allow me to say in summary: This is good Masala Chai. It's a mostly balanced blend with a good mix of quality ingredients that tastes great when brewed properly; however, in its only shortcoming, the flavor of actual tea is somewhat weak, likely due to the condition of the leaves in the blend, which may or may not be Rishi's fault. It's always possible the package was treated harshly in transit resulting in a can full of small leaf pieces as opposed to full leaves. I won't be able to say until I'm done with this one and get more, which I probably will do. Now only the longer version:

I've long been a fan of Masala Chai, brewing it in pots in the traditional manner at home before it became popular in cafes and giving long-winded explanations to people why the term "chai tea latte" should never be used thereafter. I prefer chai that tastes nothing like the mild, over-sweetened brews sold at most cafes in this country. Instead, ones like those found at authentic Indian restaurants have been my preference, but even then I've found many do not do as good a job with their Masala Chai as I would have liked. It is very safe to say I can be picky about my Chai. Snobbish, even. My supplier of choice for years had been a local tea artisan who mixed his own teas and made fantastic blends I've yet to find the match of. Sadly, he closed some months ago leaving the world bereft of his magnificent concoctions. This left me hunting for a new supply everywhere I could look from local tea shops, to high-end grocery stores, to the internet. This also meant I have tried a number of Chais I did not care for. Rishi's is not one of those. It is, in fact, one of the better one's I've tried.

It's made with a solid blend of ingredients. This tea suffers no "innovations" in the name of trying to distinguish itself. It's ingredients are whole and it's flavors generally balanced. It's also fairly strong. This one surprised me given the condition it seemed to be in when I opened it. I was prepared for the worst, as most of the tea leaves seemed broken into small pieces, but came out pleasantly surprised. In all, for someone looking for a good chai, this is an easy recommendation to make. Considering it won the World Tea Championship's award last year for best chai, this isn't particularly surprising, though. Also, it is certified both fair trade and organic, for whatever that is worth to you.

What is surprising is it's one weakness. As I've said, when I opened my first canister to brew a cup, I found no whole tea leaves. Instead I found many small pieces of tea leaves. From a company of Rishi's reputation this was shocking. The predictable result was the flavor of tea was weak and unbalanced compared to those of the spices, which were strong and balanced with each other well. This was a disappointment, and I expected not to care for the tea at all while it was brewing, but this proved not to be the case. Still, this may have been my favorite blend were it not for that. (As it stands the pricier Ineeka holds that spot) It's wholly possible the condition of the leaves was caused during delivery. I won't know until my next order.

Yes, "My next order." In spite of it's one real flaw, I will be placing another order. As I said, this is good tea, and really, for the price, I have not found another tea whose quality competes. Still, I will probably take the advice of some of the other reviewers and start supplementing it with some black tea leaves of my own.

I am a great fan of greens and oolongs, particularly scented teas.

This puerh brews deep reddish-brown liquor. It is a full-bodied, smooth tea. It has a light, not overbearing floral scent and a bold, but slightly sweet, fruity taste and a somewhat astringent finish.

I do not taste the green except in the finish. In fact, I wondered at first if there actually was green tea in the blend. I was also interested in what is in the teabag, so I opened one to examine it. There is indeed green tea in it. The teabag does not contain tea dust. It contains fannings, which are pieces of broken leaf.
I have added photos so you can see the liquor and the contents of the teabag.

You can drink this pleasant tea unadorned if you wish. It is a good afternoon offering and is suitable to serve with dessert. It marries very well with Dare Cookies, Lemon Creme, 12.3-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12). You can steep this tea two or three times. I brewed it at about 200 degrees Fahrenheit because green tea brews bitter in boiling water. Brew it in simmering water. I am pleasantly surprised and think this is worth trying, especially for those who want to try a new type of tea.

This rabbit product is very good, if you like hassenpfeffer. I would rate it 5 (instead of 4) if it were not so high priced and expensive to ship. Also, I had hoped to be able to use the fur to tie salmon flies -- oh well. However, I have discovered why this whole rabbit product is so expensive: These rabbits are imported from Canada!
The University of Victoria, in Victoria BC, has had a feral rabbit problem for years. Recently, they have got a lot of press because of their intentions to thin the herd (Check numerous articles in the Victoria Times-Colonist, summer to fall, 2010.) This has met with significant public resistance; plans to trap, neuter and re-release the rabbits have not gone far, either, partly because cost estimates run to $227/snip. And there are literally hundreds of the little buggers.
Using my Automatic Game & Wildlife Camera, with infrared attachment (very good on deer, BTW. I review it elsewhere,) I have documented photos of black-clad meat company representatives (I think of them as rabbit Ninjas) "harvesting" sacks full of bunnies on moonless nights. They place these sacks into a black van (with US licence plates!!) and catch the ferry back south to Washington State.
This is a pretty reprehensible business plan (although, as a starving student, I must confess to doing it as an amateur; it beats road-kill.)
The only good thing I can say is, their diet is good, healthful and natural; and they are free of hormone and antibiotic additives.

South Africans are as avid tea drinkers as the inhabitants of any other country (formerly) belonging to the British Commmonwealth - today, consumption averages about 10 billion cups per year - and tea was first grown in Durban Botanical Gardens in 1850 from plants imported from London's Kew Gardens (commercial production began in 1877, with seeds from Assam). Yet, production around the major tea center of Tzaneen in the Northern Province (formerly known as North-East Transvaal) as well as in the country's other tea growing locations has had an unstable history; staggering badly in the mid-twentieth century and although revived thereafter, available only domestically during apartheid. Only after apartheid ended, South African tea farmers were able to export their products. Hence, black tea from South Africa is still a fairly well-kept secret; although roughly 40% of the country's tea is now sold on the world market and it is already among the world's top 20 tea-producing nations.

Harvested before the beginning of the winter cool, between October and April, a tea fairly well-known outside South Africa is that produced by the Ntingwe Estate located in a remote corner of the Kwazulu-Natal heartland. Established in 1987 and with over 200 permanent employees, 430 seasonal pickers as well as a program involving the cooperation of local farmers with the estate's on-site processing plant, Ntingwe is *the* single biggest employer and source of financial stability in a region otherwise plagued by record unemployment numbers (up to 60%), illiteracy and poverty. Lighter than other African (e.g. Kenyan) teas, Ntingwe tea has gained an excellent reputation in the short time since its introduction to the international market and makes for as great a breakfast tea as an afternoon refreshment or a pick-me-up throughout the day.

Having once lived in Japan for almost ten years, I'm a bit of a noodle freak. Ramen, soba, rice, glass, pasta, every kind of noodle is my friend. These noodles looked to be a promising candidate to join my circle of noodle friends. Unfortunately, these were a bit harder to get to know than most noodles.

First of all, there is nothing on the package that tells you how to cook the noodles. There is an unhelpful (but critical) suggestion to soak the noodles in water for one minute (to soften them up), followed by two recipes. I'm assuming the recipes are a good way to enjoy the noodles (I didn't try them, however), but I just wanted to add them to some chicken soup I'd made. After soaking the noodles, I noticed that they had not gotten noticeably softer, and they were still quite bland. I decided to put them in a fry pan with some butter, and that did the trick. They softened up nicely as they absorbed the oil, and they were quite tasty after that. They were great in the soup, too. So with the preparation mystery solved, my second complaint is that the noodles are dry and very fragile coming out of the bag, and it was next to impossible to pull off a reasonable sized portion from the massive woven nest of noodles. Attempts at breaking them by hand ended with a flurry of noodle fragments all over the counter and floor (and probably the bottom of the bag of noodles, too). Same result with a knife. I suppose you could crush the bag before opening it to break up the noodles, but then where's the fun of the long, slender, slurpable noodle? I suffered through carefully pulling them apart and brushing the fragments into the pan to cook (and vacuuming the rest off the floor). But I say again, these were delicious noodles.

So here's what you've got: very tasty noodles with great texture and flavor that require experimentation to figure out how to cook and that make a mess during preparation (unless you plan to eat the whole bag all at once). I'll sum them up as "clumsily delicious" and worth three and a half, okay four, stars.

Coconut oil is a saturated fat. At first glance that alone might make dieters and the health conscious recoil in fear.  Haven't we been told that all saturated fats are artery clogging sludge?  As it turns out, coconut oil is emerging as a near miracle food. Pacific Island populations who get 30-60 percent of their total caloric intake from fully saturated coconut oil have all shown nearly non-existent rates of cardiovascular disease.  The multitude of benefits, including strengthening the immune system and regulating metabolism, make fascinating reading readily available in technical journals and web resources.  Unlike many foods considered healthy, coconut flesh is incredibly delicious.  Since most of us, though, don't relish the idea of hacking the nut to pieces with machetes in the kitchen, coconut is being made conveniently available as in this product, Coconut Manna; a combination of ground coconut flesh and associated oil.  I've been incorporating coconut oil into health shakes so was anxious to try this product which incorporated the flesh as well.  Anyone who has used coconut oil knows that it likes to congeal and form a solid at normal room temperatures and inevitably so in cool locations.  Opening this coconut manna container revealed what resembled a wad of lumpfish stuck to the walls packed in oil.  Not very appetizing.  A metal spoon employed to break it up encountered stubborn resistance.  Submerging the plastic container in warm water would have returned it to an easily workable state, but not something you typically want to do if making a quick health shake or spread.  For that it lost one or maybe one and a half points.  But that's just the natural state of the food and Nutra can't be faulted for that.  The product itself once more malleable is absolutely delicious.  It's tempting to just eat it off the spoon before it makes it to whatever vehicle you planned to park it on.  For smoothy/shake makers, the pure oil form is probably easier to use, though it can congeal also, though probably not as readily or as stubbornly as this manna. It is delicious, but only if you want to take the time to render it at a temperature to make it more easily spread and applied.

This deal on Amazon is a slightly better deal than you are likely to get on Bob's Red Mill quinoa in stores. It typically sells for $9-$11 per 26 oz bag. So this deal works out to just under $9 a bag. Unfortunately Bob's Red Mill does not sell their 25 lb bags on Amazon, which is by far their best value. If you are serious about quinoa as a staple of your diet and you'd eventually eat that much, here's the math: This deal works out to $5.53 per pound of quinoa, while bulk works out to $3.44 per pound. A skilled google searcher can find where to get it 25 lb bags of quinoa from Bob's Red Mill, but hopefully Bob's Red Mill and Amazon will work out a way to sell them through Amazon.

Like most people, I have been a fan of chocolate for probably my whole life. However, as I have grown older, I have found that dark chocolate gives me the intensity of flavor that gives me my fix. It all started, of course, with Hershey's Special Dark chocolate, which now tastes way too sweet for my palate. Through the years there was Ghiardelli and some of the Belgian companies. Then I discovered Scharffen Berger chocolate which I found to be as good or better than the European varieties in taste, with the added benefit of being an American company interested in fair trade and who are ecologically green.

Through my research on the internet, I stumbled on this article about a small italian chocolate company, Amadei, who took on and beat French goliath Valhrona chocolates for trade with farmers in a precious region of Venezuela, where both chuao and porcialana beans are grown. Well, needless to say, I got my hands (and mouth) on this chocolate and it was truly a wonderful experience. These are single bean chocolates which allow the lucky eater to taste the subtle differences in flavors that exist in the actual chocolates themselves: from different types of fruits like cherry or banana, to nuts, spices, tobacco, coffee, and caramel.

I have given this product, and all of the other wonderful products that Amadei makes, only 4 stars for two reasons: cost and convenience. Regardless of whether you order it through Amazon or directly from their website, it takes forever for them to process the order, usually 4 or 5 business days. You can have it sent standard which takes another 7 to 10 days after processing the order (for a fairly heavy fee), or expedited which takes 'only' 3 to 5 days after processing the order for even more money. Either way, you need to be patient. (I am wondering if they have heard about airplanes at Amadei!) By the way, shipping times that I quoted are to California. The cost of this product is the other big issue. It is perhaps the most expensive chocolate available. The three 50 gram (slightly more than 2 oz.) bars I recently purchased cost $58 dollars after shipping and handling, almost $20 per bar. (They are listed at an already steep price of $14 per bar.) Here's the rub: Valhrona Noir or their Extra Noir chocolates are truly fantastic and definitely competes for flavor and texture to Amadei, even though they are not single bean origin. Additionally, there are so many fine chocolate companies that have their single bean chocolates available in grocery stores here in the US, and some are very good to excellent as well.

You'll have to decide if its worth it. If you are a serious chocolate afficianado, or just a plain old junky, buy a lot of Amadei's chocolate at one time, to defray the cost of shipping (they have multi-kilogram bags of their chocolate in little bit-sized squares.) Or just go exploring the wonderful world of chocolate in your local specialty store.

I selected Marley Coffee & Tea One Love Organic Coffee, 15-Count based solely on a five sentence blurb in the amazon.com/VINE offering to me in its monthly newsletter to sample and to review. There were no instructions on how to prepare the brew. I did not worry. I expected the shipped coffee to contain enough instructions on arrival. It did not.

If, however, I had gone to the non-VINE website of Amazon I would have received a clue how to brew the coffee: "Directions
For Use only in Single Serve Home Coffee Pod Brewers."

I don't own a "single server home coffee pod brewer," so the test was going to prove difficult at best, although I did not think so at the time.

Then came in the mail an attractively packaged, colorful cardboard box, full of small print texts extolling various aspects of the product with Lion of Judah logo, photo of a Rastafarian man and a statement from musician Bob Marley about how he had founded his organic coffee and tea company as a tribute to his father who had come from Nine Mile, Jamaica.

Very instructive. But no brewing instructions anywhere. I scissored open the air-sealed plastic cover for one of the 15 small pods enclosed of ground coffee. No instructions.

Here are the various ways I went about making Marley coffee:

(1) Were these 15 like similar pods I had seen in motels with DIY coffee makers?Where you toss pods in a plastic filter and add hot water into the back of the machine. Then throw a switch. Expect two cups of coffee to emerge. So I scissored open four plastic bags, detecting in the process a beyond faint aroma that I had years earlier come to associate with kidneys for breakfast in bed and breakfasts in Ireland. I tossed four pods into my Mr. Coffee MachineMr. Coffee CG12 12-Cup Switch Coffeemaker, White and added enough water in my to make eight cups of coffee. No paper filter. Result: tasty, several ingredients detected. Very weak!

(2) After discussion with my wife, I next decided to make a mere two cups of coffee using only two pods in Mr. Coffee, this time placing a paper filter beneath the pods. Same initial urine smell. Same good taste. Stronger.

(3) Still my wife and I, in the absence of written instructions, decided there must be a simpler, cleaner way. We next treated a pod as if it were a single serving tea bag -- minus a string. We therefore put one pod in a coffee mug and poured boiling water over it. Same Irish kidneys smell. Decent taste when done. Rather a mess, however, fishing out the pod with a spoon.

Bottom line: even when weak, Marley Coffee & Tea One Love Organic Coffee, 15-Count offered a strikingly better than average taste. I would drink it again if only I had the right equipment.

I am new to matcha tea (this was my first) but I am very happy with Malden's powdered green tea. I bought it based on the other positive reviews and a little research, and was very pleased. Sixteen bucks for 1/2 a pound puts it in a league of its own. Most of the other matcha powders are much more expensive. I've been drinking it daily for over two weeks (even sharing it with others) and still have well over half of it left.

Now if the matcha quality wasn't good then it wouldn't be worth it. After the sensory overload of my very first cup, I learned to prepare it properly and have grown to really enjoy the taste and extended "lift" it provides. It might not be "ceremonial" grade, but it blends well, has a lovely green color and has a bright, fresh flavor. Some people have said it has a fishy smell but I don't detect that. It is really more akin to freshly mowed grass. The added bonus is the health benefits associated with consuming the whole tea leaf -- win win!

I highly recommend getting a bamboo whisk and proper matcha bowl, but for quick office preparation, some hot water in a mug and a small spoonful works fine. Just be sure to stir it up a lot, and re-stir if you let it sit for a minute or two. It isn't bad with a little vanilla creamer and honey/sugar in the raw either. Matcha may not be to everyone's taste, but for those that enjoy it, Malden's bulk Matcha Powder is hard to beat.

This is coconut butter, not coconut cream or coconut milk. It's dried white coconut meat that's been ground to a spreadable consistency, like nut butter. The fat in coconut solidifies at temps below 76 degrees. So that's why most people have to warm it up to use it. I keep it in a sealed plastic baggie and put it a bowl or sink of hot water for a few minutes to make it spreadable.
WHY I use it: Coconut oil contains fatty acids that kill bacteria, viruses and fungus. I take it to control the fungus that causes yeast infections (candida). One tablespoon of coconut butter or oil contains one gram of caprylic acid. That's a lot of tablets OR one tablespoon of coconut butter or oil, which I find easier to take. It's not only helped control the candida, but I've also noticed my immune system is stronger. I've used coconut oil for about a year, and my rate of colds/sinus infections has dropped by 80%. The one cold I did catch was much less severe and I recovered in half the time.
HOW I use it: with green curry paste to make Thai dishes, or to make a white sauce with nutmeg for vegetables. I also use it to make a creamy, sugar-free treat to take the place of the ice cream I gave up (had to give up sugar b/c it feeds candida). I melt one tablespoon of this product, mix it into an 8 ounce serving of nonfat Greek yogurt, sweeten with your favorite sugar-free sweetener and chill.
