It seems like another new type of nutrition bar, energy bar, or diet bar pops up every week. I can't even count the number of brands, let alone varieties. A lot of them are loaded with sugar, and in many cases you might be better off just eating an apple or a banana and a handful of nuts, but they are really convenient to have around. They keep for a long time, have interesting and varied flavors, and are certainly much better for you than most any candy bar.

To compete in such a crowded market, these products need some sort of differentiator to set them apart from the crowd. In the case of "Eat. Think. Smile." from Apure foods (a Colorado subsidiary of Hershey's) it's the Cocoa Lavado, which they claim has much higher levels of antioxidants in comparison to common Dutch processed cocoa. Such flavonoids might be good for your heart and circulatory system and could potentially even lower cancer risk a tiny bit.

There have been at least a couple of studies indicating there may well be health benefits to lavado "washed" cocoa, including one last year from Pennsylvania State University that showed the higher levels of polyphenols in this type of cocoa appear to help block carbohydrates and fats, potentially helping manage weight.

I was curious how much of this cocoa is in each bar, in comparison to how much would be needed for any health benefits to be fully realized. A Hershey study cited by Eat. Think. Smile. seemed to indicate that consuming 22g of natural cocoa was found to cause a measureable improvement in blood vessel health, but I couldn't easily find how many grams of cocoa these bars actually contain. I'll have to assume for now that they contain at least enough to provide some potential benefit.

So, is it enough? I had to also evaluate the taste, price, and other factors to help find out.
At over a dollar per bar, these certainly aren't cheap, but also not out of line with other nutrition bars on the market. I don't know how much it costs to make one of these or a PowerBar or Cliff Bar, etc, but I suspect they must be rather profitable, as evidenced by the crowded market, and yet still fairly steady prices. I must be in the wrong line of work.

As for ingredients and nutrition, these certainly aren't for the allergy-prone, as they contain nuts, milk, wheat, corn, and eggs. As long as that's not a problem, they seem reasonably balanced from a nutritional perspective with mostly natural ingredients, including the cocoa, and without a bunch of extra vitamins artificially crammed in for show. They have 200 calories, 4g protein, and 6g of fiber, much of it from chicory root extract (for comparison Fiber One bars, which are a little smaller, have about 140 calories, 2g protein, and 9g of fiber).

I found the Dark Cherry flavor nutrition bars to have a nice flavor, fairly sweet, but not overpoweringly so, with a somewhat light and vaguely cakelike texture (at least in comparison to heavy protein and sports nutrition bars). The cherry bits, nuts, and oats seemed well balanced without overpowering the cocoa flavor, and as nutrition bars go, these tasted pretty good.

Would I buy more? Probably, if they go on sale. I do like them better than some other bars, and I also like the idea of the natural, minimally processed cocoa, but I still think the whole product category is overpriced so I tend to either look for good deals, or I find alternate snacks (for example the aforementioned fresh fruit and nuts). It's hard to beat the convenience of bars you can just drop in a backpack or desk or locker for when you need them though, and these seem as good as most and better than many.

My cat gets so impatient with me whilst I am trying to empty the entire packet into her food bowl--she makes it really difficult by pushing her head in the way and meowing loudly.

All in all though, my cat loves these and I love that my cat is so happy to eat them.

This is an interesting new product from the makers of Splenda and quite frankly I'm surprised it took so long for this combination to come out on the market.
Splenda, in general, is used by many health fanatics to cut down on soluble sugar without sacrificing the sugar taste since it's made from actual sugar instead of aspartame or saccharine. Add a gram of fiber to each packet since fiber is another critical ingredient to healthy living and ridiculously hard to come by (Often 1 gram per slice of bread and you should have 24 grams per day) if you're actually paying attention, and you have a recipe for good sense and taste.

This product tastes the same as your usual Splenda and is highly soluble in hot beverages. The thing I like about Splenda is that it is typically soluble in cold liquids as well, however you have to stir for a while for this to dissolve in cold beverages. In fact, if you're drinking clear cold or translucent cold liquids, once you add the Splenda with fiber, you might think there is gunk and debris in your drink. Since the packet contents looks just like Splenda with fine powdery sugar, I thought my drink was contaminated after I poured it in my iced tea, since random chunks appeared in my drink. After about a minute or so, it finally dissolved and looked normal again.

Last, but certainly not least, if you like to throw packets of sweetener in your purse or pocket, the packaging for each serving is very durable. The inner contents is lined with an almost foil so the light paper packing doesn't rip or tear accidentally. This is handy if you carry your sweetener with you for travel purposes. Overall, it's a healthy and convenient combination, especially if you're looking to add more fiber to your diet. The only thing where the jury is out on, is if price point reflects the innovation since it is more expensive than standard Splenda.

I added both peas and broccoli and was pleasantly suprised to find that the cheese sauce was plentiful enough for all of the pasta, peas, and broc.  I also must say, as my first time trying to cook gluten-free pasta on my own, this was painless and didn't crumble apart (like it could have).  I gave it 4 stars, not quite perfect, but definitely a great treat (every once in awhile, for those of us on a budget).

Wow!!!! This is really sweet but very good.  Make sure, if you are diabetic, to drink only 1/4 to 1/2 a bottle a day.  THE TASTE is out of this world.  I like it, but it is very sweet.  Try it at least once!

I like this coffee. It is NOT a French roast but as another reviewer said it is Bold and has some good flavor with no "off" tastes. The beans are roasted to a dark brown, not the oily black, typical of a french roast. Yet it is similar to a french roast with a nice strong flavor

I was very disappointed with another Boyer's selection - their "Denver" blend - which I found so bland that it was almost tasteless.

This is a great buy and I would recommend it. The vacuum sealing seemed far better this time when compared to the Boyer's "Denver" blend I tried a month earlier.

A minor point - the bag is not as easily resealable as most bulk packaged coffees and you may want to store it in a container rather than trying to reseal the bag.

When a shampoo is really creamy I tend to think it is going to weigh down my hair. Such was not the case with this luxuriously lathering shampoo. It deep cleaned my hair and scalp and seemed to leave each strand a little more nourished. After I blowdried my hair I could really see an increase in volume. My hair was also shiny and quite bouncy. One thing I noticed while using this shampoo is that you need less conditioner. I also had to learn to use much less shampoo than I normally use. Just a quarter size amount in your palm is all you really need. The mild floral scent is also lovely.

~The Rebecca Review

This brew is typical of the Coffee Bean Direct. It is bold with no bad after-taste.
The price is a right for this quailty of coffee. There are better blends at a much
higher price, but at this price point you can't go wrong.

According to Wiki, Scharffen Berger was an independent chocolate producer in the San Fransisco Bay area that was acquired by the Hershey Company in 2005. Scharffen Berger continues to produce chocolate under this name, now at a plant in Illinois. Its products include the Bittersweet Dark Chocolate Bar reviewed here.

Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate is 70% cocoa and is considered "bittersweet", with a much stronger chocolate taste than milk chocolate that most Americans consume. Though this is definitely a rich dark chocolate, I was actually a bit surprised by how smooth the Scharffen Berger chocolate was; though there is the slightest hint of bitterness, it is less than other 70% chocolate bars I have tried before. If anything, as person who admires dark chocolate I wish that the Scharffen Berger had a bit more character; it is very good and very smooth but isn't memorable to me like their Scharffen Berger Mocha (Dark Chocolate with Freshly Roasted Coffee) Chocolate Bar (62% Cacao) is.

In any event, Scharffen Berger Bittersweet Dark Chocolate is still a fine product that I will enjoy whenever I have the chance to have some.

I really like Emerald's packaging for their nuts -- it fits nicely in your hand. All the easier to indulge in over-eating! It's nice to throw in my daughter's backpack for a snack on the go.

As far as the salt and pepper cashews go, the adults in the house loved them but not a big hit with the kids. The pepper was too much for them. I loved the pepper but thought there was too much salt. This product claims to be a healthy snack, but I think it would be healthier with about half the salt. Don't get me wrong, they taste great as is, I just won't eat as much at one time since I'm concerned about too much salt in my diet. For me it's a guilty pleasure!

The order came in a timely fashion & in its own cooler with dry ice.
My wife loves dark chocolate & is more or less a connoisseur. She gave it her highest praise.

Very good. I put 4 tablespoons of this in my single cup coffee maker and it tastes great! Not sharp or overly bitter. Just right, very mellow for being a darkest and boldest coffee they offer. I like this company and Tully's for smooth coffee over bitter and overpriced Starbucks any day!! I'll buy this again.  They've changed the label, it's not purple and red  w/ a big 5. Great coffee. I DRINK IT BLACK. It costs $5.99 or $6.99 locally.

We like to put this out in the office for the employees and customers to get.
For some reason, Hershey's puts a disproportionate amount of the nuggets to what people want. I think there's about an equal likeability for the Milk Chocolate, Milk Chocolate w/ Almonds, Dark Chocolate w/ Almonds, but no one likes the Toffee and Almonds one. Don't get me wrong (I love toffee), but there was just a big miss on their Toffee and Almond one. The bits are so small that you can't even taste them.
But other than that, the rest of the nuggets are delicious (my personal favorite is the Dark Chocolate Almond).

If you like pineapple flavor in smoothies. snow cones, mixed drinks, this is the stuff you are looking for. Great natural taste. Not quite yellow color.  Brownish yellow color,like real pineapple.  Pour out some in a glass, add a little water and yellow food dye and you have perfect yellow pinapple smoothie.  This stuff is concentrated and  potent.  A liitle amount is all that you will need for the flavor.Very sweet and high calories.

I tried these mixes because my sister likes them with her bread machine. I just get tired of having to think too much about what to put in my bread, so, a mix made sense. The yeast is really sensitive to temp, use your thermometer to be sure the water is not too hot. Reliable delicious bread or rolls with only a few minutes of effort. I want to try them all now.

I have tried several Dr. McDougall's Vegan soups with three different microwaves.  The time needed in each has been quite different - from needing less (to avoid boiling over) to needing more.  The soup should to be very hot but not hot enough to boil over.  I believe many complaints of "chewy" pasta/noodles/veggies is probably from unwillingness to experiment with cooking and standing times.

When I saw this product on the supermarket shelf my curiosity was piqued both by the name and the claim they would release energy throughout the morning and keep me from becoming hungry. I bought one box - at a lower price than the Amazon price because it was a featured item - and began my experiment. I'm very happy to say that I'm impressed.

I have now finished the five packets in the box (with four breakfast biscuits per packet) and can say they taste very good and definitely do work. I have one packet of the biscuits, a serving of yogurt and a piece of fresh fruit and this combination holds me for at least four hours, often past that if I'm super busy. I like the crispness of the biscuits and the fact that they were all completely whole in their packets yet not hard. The flavor of cinnamon brown sugar was not overwhelmingly sweet, just enough for that tiny satisfying taste. From a nutritional standpoint, the four biscuits contain 230 calories, 80 of which come from fat. There is no high fructose corn syrup, hydrogenated oils or artificial flavors or sweeteners. They contain 3g dietary fiber (12% daily need) and 8g total fat (also 12%).

For a convenient way to satisfy your breakfast-on-the-go, this product is quite outstanding. Just remember that you do need to add other healthy items to make them a totally nutritional breakfast. I'm definitely looking forward to trying other flavors.

I do wonder about the name though. At first I thought it was some weird take-off on a well known cheese-like product!!

I am giving this four stars because the taste is somewhat delicate.  Perhaps the reason is it being decaf.  I usually have a couple of cups with a bit of cream and Splenda a day.  It's a nice switch from coffee; chill it in the fridge for a refreshing Spring/Summer drink.  Overall, for the excellent price and availability, I am a happy consumer.
Wow these are awesome... they are a little expensive for what you get but they are pretty good for a snack of something very very healthy.

Yes they have 520 cal per pouch and yes there are 160 cal from fat, 40g of carbs and 1220mg of sodium all things that should be consumed in moderation.  However, for me it is a quick easy meal and covers one meal a day.  I actually prefer the picante ones better but these are a good change-up.  Deployed it is nice to have something tasty I can eat in just a few minutes and the calories and fat can be burnt off in no time

These are pretty good.

The cans are well filled with product, and not too much water. The cans have a pull-top which is easy to open.

The artichokes do appear to be young, smaller ones and, rather surprisingly, the gentle aromas and flavor complexities of that still comes across, even in the canned product. They all have an even, healthy color without bruising or other blemishes. While it's true that all canned foods are going to taste "canned", these are much less noticeable in that regard than any other artichokes packed in water that I've purchased. The flavor is good, as is the texture. They are quite tender, not mushy, but you can easily smoosh them for puree or bruschetta or what you will.

They are quartered pieces, easy to use as-is or chop as desired. I have had to remove what I consider to be some tough bits and outer leaves. Maybe these weren't bad enough to bother other people. I've had much worse from canned artichokes!

They do not lend a canned/metallic flavor to other ingredients, nor are they too salty, oily, vinegary, bitter, stale, or any of the other unpleasant flavors that one often gets with canned artichokes. Cooked as an addition to other dishes they contribute appealingly.
I'll keep the review simple. I plan to order more of this coffee blend today. Smooth, satisfying brew. Good value.

If you need a gluten free mix this one is VERY good. The best price I've found is on Amazon.
People who do not need to be gluten free eat and enjoy it. No one suspected there was a difference.

I love this coconut oil and I continue to order it regularly, but for health purposes, I wish it came in a glass jar. If it did, I'd give it 5 stars. I also wish it were cold pressed.

Please consider glass?

I eat Raisin Bran regularly, so I was interested in trying the Cinnamon and Almond version. I was not disappointed.

Some cereals overcompensate with their flavoring, but the cinnamon seems just right. It isn't overpowering at all. The almonds didn't add much to the flavor, but I'm an almond fan. The flakes stayed crunchy in milk long enough for me to finish most of it before they got soggy.

I'm also in medicine, and while cereal alone isn't the best breakfast, this version of Raisin Bran is good enough to be part of a healthy breakfast. There is a good amount of fiber, with relatively low levels of sodium and sugar.

There are so many variations of cereal out there, and I usually buy the bagged versions to save money, but I will make an exception to have this one as a special treat from time to time.

I have been looking for organic San Marzano tomatoes for some time and now I have it! Thanks so much. I have two issues, though.

1. It was not clear to me prior to my purchase that these cans already have "BASIL LEAF" in them and I would not have preferred that as I add my own fresh basil

2. Two of the cans were pretty dented--do you think this is a problem? Or...was it damaged in transit. It was double boxed.

Otherwise I will be making several batches of marinara sauce.

Being a lover of fresh food, I prefer cooking a fresh batch of rice for any meal. But, sometimes I feel lazy or I'm just so f'ing hungry I can't wait 30-40 minutes for the rice cooker. I was skeptical about buying microwaveable rice but Nishiki is a good brand so I gave it shot. Glad I did. It's quick, has just the right portion, and it's actually pretty good. I make sure to always have a pack of these in my pantry.

It's not easy for us to find items that everyone in the family likes. We have one very picky eater, and another "sort of" picky eater. One of them never liked Cheez-its ever (the regular kind) but was willing to try one of these. They all liked it!

The mozarella flavor is mild, and not overwhelming. It makes for a perfect flavor enhancer to the standard Cheez-It cracker.

Only problem is that it is seasoned with MSG (monosodium glutamate). This is something asthmatics are told to avoid, and with three asthmatics in the family, it can't be on our grocery list, unfortunately.

We all enjoyed the flavor though, and think most other folks will too.

For the amount of money spent on this product I really feel like I got a good value.  The tiramisu was surprisingly good.  rich, flavorful, and moist.  I most definitely be interested in repeat business and recommend this product to all of my friends.  Thanks D'Italia!
Very good coffee w/ a very nice flavor.  Not too bold, not too mild.  I will buy this coffee again.

I have to admit that I read several consumer reviews prior to tasting this tea and I was still not prepared for the strong, unusually smokey flavor! It is definitely an acquired taste and if you like smoked products like smoked bacon, almonds or smoked Gouda in particular...you will get used to the unique, smokey taste of this tea.  I began drinking it by itself and then halfway through added some milk, which toned down the intense smokiness a bit.  I can't say I could drink this as easily as I do Earl Grey which I could drink all day long, but there will be days I would definitely be in the mood.  As a final note, all throughout the experience, I wanted to eat smoked almonds! ;-)

This is a very tasty and spicy beverage, which may not be your cup of tea, so to speak. The smell of ginger is strong when opening the pouch and the taste is rather strong and piquant. For many people not used to a strong ginger flavor, this may be off-putting and even unpleasant. If your idea of ginger stops at Canada Dry ginger ale, you will probably not like this product. I grew up with ginger in my foods, so I love this! The closest thing I can compare this to is Indonesian Ting Ting Jehe Chewy Ginger Candy. This is basically a liquid version of the candy. Very sweet and spicy, it tickles the throat going down. I've juiced fresh ginger root (with other ingredients) and this tastes like the ginger-infused juice I've made. The pungency is not diminished during manufacturing.

Served hot, it is perfect when you're sick. I often make ginger tea with honey when I'm under the weather, and this is a more convenient way of having a tasty hot beverage. Ginger and honey both have been used for thousands of years throughout the world for their health and medicinal benefits. The lemon flavor I couldn't detect however.

Got this for a friends daughter after surgery. She loved it and had to hide it from the rest of the family!  My only, minor, complaint is that it took longer than I thought for delivery. It may have even said it on the site, but I didn't pay attention so I can not fault them. I am used to having ANYTHING I buy on Amazon come pretty much immediately, but this took almost a week. (including the weekend)  Just remember to order it a good week in advance of when you need it and it'll be fine.
Quick and easy, a hurry up solution to what to have for dinner. Kept my chops moist, provided good flavor. Good job.

Update:after a week or so of drinking this, I decided to stop because I was having some odd health problems (upset stomach, etc) and a lot more sinus/allergy problems than normal. I decided that it might be the Acai berries, that were causing the problem. I looked on the internet and the berries are associated with some stomach problems. I really did like it, especially diluted somewhat, but it's not worth the aggravation. If you don't think allergies will be a problem, here's what I thought of the product:

I decided to try this flavor additive for bottles of water because it is decaf and also, unlike most of those flavor-adds, it does not use Equal or some other sweetener. I can't drink much caffeine at one time (more than a couple of sips can really mess me up) and I also can't use Equal or several other of the sweeteners. This tea uses honey and the natural sweetness of the strawberries and the Acai berries to sweeten the green tea that is the basis of the beverage and it doesn't contain caffeine. It mixed very easily with the water and had a nice taste. I don't like my bottled water to have very much flavor, so I tried changing the ratio (it was one packet to each 16.9 bottle) to see how using half strength would work and I liked that even better. I ended up just putting the bottle of water with the flavor in it inside my fridge door and I just get a glass of water from a plain bottle and then add however much of the flavor that I want. My boss liked the flavor, too, when I gave him a glass full. I wasn't sure how to tell the Acai berries from the green tea, but I could definitely taste the strawberry, so if you don't like strawberries, you probably need to skip this product. But if you love them, maybe you've found this year's summer drink.
These peppers are the hottest thing I have ever eaten! I live hot stuff and they were too much for me to handle!

The quality of the shipment and it's contents was great and on time.  There were no problem with the order.  I can't give it an excellent rating, though, just due to the fact of its contents.  Not that I did ot know that a the time of purchase.  It a grossly proceessed food, which is probably why I like it.  I'm the only one eating them in the houe and they're just about Finished.
Everything you need to get started. You can feel and taste the quality. My only concern is the sushi roll mat. The string seems to be wearing/threading out. I don't expect it to last long.

This tea is pretty good, but definitely not the best jasmine pearl tea I've had.

Unfortunately this is actually only "jasmine scented" according to the package itself.

I do appreciate the fact that it is organic tea, and the taste is good.

For the price, the tea is a good purchase, but I would suggest spending a little bit more and getting a better tasting tea.

We have been eating basmati rice as our daily staple for over 25 years.  After trying this rice because of the reviews, and because our local supermarket was out of Royal Basmati Rice, we grade this rice very good.  However we judge Royal Basmati Rice to be slightly more flavorful and has a superior texture.

we bought this food at the grocery store when we couldn't get to our regular pet store for the food we had been using.  the dog loved it, so we continued to buy this instead of the old.  I love the amazon subscription option, it has made it much easier to always have food on hand.

This is a very healthy breakfast food and well balanced, for me it need a little more sweetness to it, so i add a little honey or cutt up banana. But its great. Takes a little longer to cook because of the sun flower seeds not as quick as the instant oats, but it is healthier and has more nutritious things in it. this is a very good cat food, shredded meat and gravy, my cats really like it
no problems, with delivery or product, I recommend it highly
This olive oil is a good value for the price but is nothing spectacular.  It has fairly good olive oil flavor which is easily overshadowed by a good balsamic vinegar.

I use a Keurig brewer, so when I brew this coffee I just snip open a pouch and dump it into my Ekobrew (reusable, refillable coffee cup for Keurig brewers).

This is good, strong coffee. The sticker says "exotic floral and berry". I didn't detect this, really -- It has a bold flavor and you can definitely taste the medium roast. I'm not a coffee connoisseur (just drink it because it tastes good, and wakes me up), but I think this stuff has good flavor.

I like this stuff because it's organic, Fair Trade, and the Marley coffee company also kicks back some of the proceeds from coffee sales to a cool sports-themed children's charity.

It's a bit expensive for my taste, but it's flavorful and ethically produces by a hip company. So give it a shot!

Not much surprise here. They fit on the bottle perfectly, the look as pictured, and they work just as you'd expect. My only complaint are that the syrup tends to crystallize on the tip causing less to pump out than when I first started the bottle, and that the syrup comes out so forcefully that you have to be careful to avoid over-spray messes.

This orange flower water is pretty good. You have to be very careful and start with just a tad and then taste and if it needs more, add it in very small amounts. If you do this, you will get a taste kind of similar to the real orange flowers, but not exactly the same. But overall, you do get a pleasant taste if you are careful.Orange Flower Water 16 oz.
Silks vanilla flavor has as a more sugary taste than Blue Diamond vanilla. I prefer Blue Diamond, but overall a good milk.

These work just fine in my Keurig and are much more reasonable than typical K-cups.  Because it is a French roast, the aroma is strong, and the coffee is quite flavorful--much more like "real" coffee than decaf.  I'm very pleased.

My nephew seems to enjoy these purees. My only comments are:

- it is a bit watery. If it was slightly thicker, it would make feeding much easier as it would be much easier to get it into his mouth. To make it thicker, I blend the puree with a little banana or steamed yams to give it a thicker consistency and make it easier to eat.

- Another note is that each pouch is so large. The instructions indicate to use within 24 hours of opening. In my nephew's case, he's 6 months old. There is no way he will be able to finish a single 4.5oz pouch in 24 hrs in addition to drinking his milk. I have had no problems with using the packs over 2-3 days.
Good sack o' nuts with a nice twist of cocoa. Wish it was more 'clustery' but eh. Nice snack throughout the day.

I bought this to dip by french bread or italian bread. It is very good for that. Has a nice garlic flavor. You can also cook with it, but I would rather save it as a dipping oil. I would purchase this again as the price is right. Usually good oils cost twice as much.

I know why the last reviewer didn't like this popcorn.  It's make with canola oil which definitely has a different smell and taste. It's pretty tasty though and I got past the initial different smell. I originally bought this to try because I have family with heart issues and canola oil is supposed to be more heart healthy than other types of oil. So, if you're looking for a healthier popcorn that doesn't use coconut or vegetable or hydrogenated oils, this one is pretty good.

A great way to try a variety of flavors without buying a full box. A nice selection of
flavors and brands to enjoy.

The dates were fine, but note that the packaging was rectangular, not round.
Since we were sending these on, this required repacking to fit the gift tin.
Not an issue if you're taking the dates out of the packaging anyway, but FYI...

I bought this by looking at all the other reviews thinking this stuff will be the equivalent to sugar, but more healthy like Agave Nectar "Not". I made a glass of tea & I tried a tablespoon & I could not tell even that I put it in, then I put in 2nd tablespoon & again nothing, then 3rd & same then fourth & it was the same, the only difference was now my tea was ruined because it was nothing but undissolved date sugar floating in my tea cup & the water was very hot so this stuff should have dissolved, but no not at all. I think this stuff would be good for things like instead of using white powdered sugar, use date sugar because it is not that sweet. It's all good because I also use other healthy sugar alternatives like ( raw organic Agave Nectar, raw organic honey & organic sugar cane sugar. Packaging was not bad, but for the price I did not expect anything special. It is another healthy option, but not for me because I want something that dissolves & something you can actually use in place of sugar & this was not doing it for me. 4 tablespoons & no change just swimming date grounded powder floating in cup. If your a light sugar type person then this may be what your looking for, but if you are a normal sugar type person that likes to actually taste there tea, then this may not be for you.

Update July 24,2012:
I updated my 2 stars to 4 stars because I found a wonderful use for this date sugar & it is in smoothies it works perfectly & now I am going to purchase more for that reason & I will try to make other things like cookies, brownies & other sweet goodies. Now that I have found a use for it, it works into my healthier diet really well. I think it was because I actually grounded it into what ever I was blending which made the dried date sugar blend very well. Now I am thinking of taking my tea & putting date sugar in & then blending it in my magic bullet or main blender & seeing if that helps with the tea situation & I know that sounds silly & weird, but it worked for the smoothies & it just may work for everything else. Plus there is nothing better to sweeten something like dates or organic natural fruits, rather then using regular sugar. So worth a try in my book & if it does not work I will still continue to use it for other stuff & also use the date sugar for sure for my smoothies & hopefully future other things. Will see!

I am making the swich from other no calorie sweeteners and bought this to use in my coffee in the morning. They recomend 6 drops as a serving and I find this to sweet so use 4 for a large cup of coffee and find it is just right! At first I found all stevia products to be a little bitter after taste but after using for a couple of weeks I am now used to it, so if you want to make the swich, just think of it as good for you and try to get used to it. It is worth the effort and you will be doing your body good!

I love Earl Grey tea--long before the Captain of the Enterprise made famous those words: "Earl Grey, hot." I have had some lovely Earl Greys over the year but have wanted a decaf version. Enter Twinings Lady Grey tea.

Lady Grey is a very pleasant tea. It is smooth and has a very mild taste. I did find that I need to use 2 bags in my mug to get that nice flavor--I suspect that one bag would be sufficient if you use an actual 4-6 oz tea cup.

Unfortunately, the mildness was just a bit too mild for me. I prefer a more robust bergamot flavor to my tea and will order the decaf Earl Grey next time.

I've also tried the fettuccine and was not very happy with those as they do not absorb pasta sauce at all. The rice shape is easier to use in a meal. I made shrimp with vegetables curry and the rice went well with it. These various forms of the noodles are great since they are carb free and do fill you up but in my experience about an hour or 2 later I am starving because my body realizes I've tricked it or because the noodles digest quickly.

These are pretty tasty, if you like the taste of Merlot that is. I feared that the taste would be over powering, but to my surprise it was subtle flavor that that was just right. Now I don't think you would want to eat them all the time but for special occasions with friends it's great, and it also makes for a nice conversation snack.

I've always, ALWAYS loved Skittles! They are sweet and chewy, and they will give you plenty of cavities if you're not careful! ^_^

Enjoy them, and buy this 3.5 lb bag today!

4.5 stars.

This product is great for a variety of purposes. I tried it to keep my hair from frizzing and to help with a dry scalp. It works well for both purposes! although this isn't a perfect cup of cocoa, it's far superior to the others that i have tried. i will order this again.
Such wonder flavors added to your home made sushi; but this stuff is expensive considering the size. However, I'd still buy it again.
Its a nice tea and I add honey to it.  It could be mintier though.
It's just got that great.  Of course it's very good, it's Belgian chocolates, but I've had better.

I have to eat gluten free, and a lot of snacks are just not very tasty. These are excellent tasting, and the ingredients are some of the best foods you can eat. I deducted one star for "Made in China". However, I have never had better tasting "processed" food.

All the flavors are tasty.

The bars' cost is on par with other, less enjoyable snacks.

They are my go to snack when I am away from home. They taste so good that I had to review them, and I almost never write reviews.

I sought this one out because I like Melinda's and I like that it contains peppers, not extracts.

It's good - first jolokia sauce I've tried. I've had a few of Melinda's habanero sauces and like them very much - definitely my favorite brand. But I think Melinda's carrot, etc. blend matches much better with habanero than jolokia - they seemed to clash a little bit. Seems the jolokia overpowered the other flavors rather than blending.

Definitely hot. Worth a try. Melinda's fans may be a bit disappointed.

It's difficult to find ground vanilla beans locally that don't have added ingredients, so it's nice that Amazon has a couple of brands to choose from. I tried this brand because of the generally positive reviews and the relatively low price.

I must say that while I think this product is good, it isn't great. I had a little bit of ground vanilla powder left that I had purchased at a local store a year or so ago, made by Madecasse. (I see that Amazon has a listing for whole beans by Madecasse, but the ground beans seem to be no longer available -- even on the manufacturer's website -- and some Amazon Marketplace seller is trying to get over $100 per ounce for it!) I must say that the Madecasse beans, grown in Madagascar, have a better aroma and flavor than this brand. This brand, grown in Papua New Guinea, is a little harsh in both aroma and taste when compared directly to Madecasse's product. Note that I only felt this way when doing a side by side comparison, however; with more time separating the two products, I quite enjoyed the aroma and taste of these beans.

Since I seldom bake anymore, my principal use for vanilla beans is to put a little bit, along with some sweetener, in some Greek yogurt. Delicious!

This chocolate is very creamy and delicious either raw or melted. It is only 54% cacao, which is either very good or not so good, depending on your preferences.

My wife and I love dark chocolate, and try to make our chocolate desserts (such as brownies, ganache, mousse, and chocolate buttercream frosting) as chocolaty as possible. This chocolate might not have enough punch for us, compared to the
Ghirardelli 60% and 70% cacao (bittersweet) chocolate that we usually buy. This chocolate is not as intensely chocolaty as either of those, and is sweeter and more creamy. I enjoy milk chocolate (which has much less cacao than dark chocolate) more than my wife does, and liked this chocolate more than she did.

This is a very good start if you are just getting into dark chocolate, though, or are already sure of what cacao level you prefer.

The original flavor would work fine with any dip and are okay on their own
The salt and pepper flavor is AWESOME. Really tasty and a great snack for only 100 calories
The sour cream and onion is a little chemicall-y but decent.
The barbeque is good but not tasty enough. The flavor doesn't go as well with the texture.

Haven't yet tried the other two flavors. Will update as I do.

If you haven't tried popchips they are sort of a cross between pringles and rice cakes. Less like styrofoam than rice cakes and made with the same potato flakes kind of texture as pringles without as much fat.

So far I have this on subscribe and save and will keep that subscription active. These definitely beat a 150 - 300 calorie bag of potato chips as a snack.

This may not be the best tasting thing I have ever drank but man do I feel instant results after drinking some. I would best describe the effects as very close to the good feeling you experience when you drink coffee. I notice that my circulation feels fantastic like my whole body is warm, a very healthy dose of energy and I dont notice any jitteryness like coffee or energy drinks give you.  The only reason I didnt rate it 5 start is because a 16oz bottle is $3.00 which I think is a little steep. But for the great feeling I get when I drink some I would highly recommend it to anyone else who wants to feel a boost of energy as well as a general sense of well being.

I found this product to be consistenly very good.It is strong,very nice flavor, and it benefits from the fact that Keurig produces a very hot coffee.If you pick "dark roast" instead of "regular", it will taste even better.

I enjoy jerky and like to try new kinds and new brands. Last week at the nearby Costco, I found 16-ounce packets of Pacific Gold Teriyaki Turkey Jerky, subdivided into two 8-ounce pouches. It's good! It's tender, but chewy. It has a nice flavor, but it's a little too sweet to be ideal for me. It has a very low fat and cholesterol, but is perhaps a little high on salt. The jerky seemed good and fresh, if you can apply that word to jerky. This stuff is pretty good. I don't think it's going to last long.

Gary Peterson

This box dinner was very easy to make and had a very good flavor. I had some leftover chicken which made it much easier and faster to prepare. The only problem I had with it was the broccoli. Tiny little pieces which I probably would not use the next time. I will use fresh or frozen broccoli.

The cheese sauce was very good, but I am glad I didn't put all of it in the dish. I really liked the orzo pasta. It was very different than any of the other Kraft Velveeta products I have tried. I wish it didn't have so much sodium in it.

I felt it deserved a 4 score because of the above problems. Will try some of the other Skillet Dinner Kits though.

I was pleasantly surprised that the gum from Trident was indeed lively with a good taste. I've had Trident gum before (though I'm not much of a gum user). This gum had a hard shell (some of the Trident gum I've tried in the past came in a paper wrapper and had no candy shell), but thankfully, it was a soft gum, and did not make me concerned I was going to break a tooth when I first popped it into my mouth (I've had gum like that, especially gum containing xylitol, though I don't know if that ingredient was responsible for that factor).

I also didn't know if I could taste the 'dash' of ginseng; I couldn't, or, at least, the taste wasn't unpleasant.

The overwhelming taste one experiences is positive. I don't know if I got a burst of vitality or not, but the gum tasted good, lasted a long time, and I'd probably get this again.

Recommended for those patients who chew gum.

My household has this tea stocked up at all times.. not to say it's my favorite tea, but it's my favorite day to day tea. We tend to drink Green Tea for its health benefits and as Green Teas go this one is affordable and fairly high quality for tea bag types. A few notes.. you have to be fairly careful about steeping this tea, it doesn't have a whole lot of tolerance from "crisp and delicious" to "overpowering and slightly off-putting". I guess I attribute that to the freshness of the tea. I'm not sure. I've had a lot different results with loose tea in a ball and some herbal teas. While this tastes good when you get it right, if you forget the cup for a few minutes, it's not forgiving. That said, that's the only real drawback to this tea. Yes. I've had teas I would rate five stars, six if I could. Yes, they also cost 5-6x more than this easily for a quarter of the amount of tea. Bottom line, if you drink a lot of tea, this is a good brand to buy. If you don't drink a whole lot and would rather buy something really high quality for the few times you do partake of it, I'd look elsewhere.

This isn't the best French Roast coffee ever. (That would be Peet's, followed by Buckmaster's.) But it's consistently good, the 4-lb bag lasts us almost a month, and with the subscription price, it's competitively priced. It's shade-grown and organic and "washed in rainwater" (what OTHER kind of water is there besides seawater?) and kind to trees and good for peasants and whatnot. Free shipping with the subscription, too. And not as crackpot-y as the biodynamic variety.

Buy this!

These cookies are so special - I find myself craving them throughout the day. I bought them especially for my afternoon tea, but find them in my fingers for breakfast, after lunch, even late at night when I should not be eating cookies. Sigh. I wish the boxes were bigger so I wouldn't have to order as often.

I bought these for my step-dad for Father's Day. He really liked two of the cans, but said the Cajun variety was so spicy he had to give them away. Next time I'll see if I can opt for a version of this product that does not include the spicier varieties!

Using these bags are so much easier than grabbing grocery bags all the time.  Just clip them on your leash and go, They are the perfect size and strength. Its also nice that you dont have to worry about forgetting anything.  Definately a good product.
This stuff is ridiculously hot ! I put a mere drop in a HUGE bowl of chili and it had me running for the fridge for milk. Do not use if you have heart problems or panic attacks easily.

There was a delay in the delivery of a Valentine vase of roses to a blind lady friend I thought would enjoy the gift and she lives quite a distance from me so I ordered on amazon.com Pro Flowers a day before the 14 of February Valentine Day. Somehow the delivery date got mixed up and a delay of a day or so I was dissapointed at the service and complained. The roses btw, were very appreciated and said to be beautiful by my friend down south.I appreciate the customer service department for there evaluation of my complaint. Yes I would give this floral delivery a future transaction.
My Terrier loves these, with or without the innovative toy they are designed to go with. It is important to keep the little creatures busy and this fulfills that bill.

The litter has a strong scent to cover up odors. However, it does have a lot of dust so the cats smell like the litter when they come out of the box. I smell like the litter when i am cleaning the box! When shipped to me, the box was banged up and there was litter leaking out of the box.

I am a devout user of Gu, and had been fairly-exclusively using the Mint Chocolate flavor, but this flavor was a welcome change. So now I mix the two flavors in the box in my fridge and just grab one on my way to run or work out, and surprise myself.  I have not cared for several of the other flavors, but this one is a keeper, and gives me the same energy that the mint chocolate Gus do.

Dogs really dig these.  I like the high protein no junk approach for their treats.  They're not light "freeze dried" feel of some other protein treats.  More dense, but not tough and stringy like jerky.  Feels a tad pricey to me.

Higgins & Burke is a name in tea that had escaped me until now, but I'm glad I found it. There are teas out there that I won't return to, but this tea has what's required: body, aroma, and flavor. I waited for the first reasonably cool morning to really appreciate it, and I'm just finishing my first cup. It won't be the only one today, now that I've had it. This is a take-it-out-on-the-front-step-and-watch-the-world-go-by sort of tea. A day-off, good-music-on-the-radio tea. I guess you could say I like it.

Taste is OK, but not great. The larger bottle is good as you waste less plastic and need to purchase the product less often. But, it is not as easy to carry with you.

This does contain caffeine (which you may well want, but it's important to know). And it also has a nice amount of vitamins.

I think I'd prefer a lemon flavor to a fruit punch however.

This coffee has my favorite characteristics: medium roast and extra bold.  By the way, the ones I got are extra bold. I don't see that in the description or on the label here. It has a bit of an aftertaste, not a bad one though.

I have 3 cats and was feeding them the Pro Plan, which is a pricey food when you consider the poor ingredients.  I am currently feeding a combination of this food, Wellness and Trader Joes. My local pet store sells this for the same price as Wellness though, and Wellness has no grains so I may switch to that as this does contain some. Ingredient list very similar to Traders Joes Turkey and Giblets formula at 69 cents a can. This is the only formula of theirs that does not contain brewers rice. They say that right on the advertising but it seemed like a great quantity for the price as well. Thanks again amazon

My 13-year-old daughter has decided that she likes granola. She's been happy to help me finish off this bag, and it's a good a snack as any for her.

I like that it's not too sweet, and has some of the less-common good-for-you grains like Flax.

In addition to eating it straight out of the bag, I tried it with milk, and it was good.

We had to guess how many for a full pot, but we decided that one per cup would do the trick. It did and we were very happy with the results. The only downside is that if they had some good instructions on how to brew a single cup included they would most likely have higher sales. The roast is really full flavored and delicious.

I'll preface my review by saying that I generally give 5 stars to products I consider "best of," hpwever, the can aside, it is not the best coffee I have had (I am something of a coffee fiend, and personally partial to African varietals and single estate coffees). It is the best coffee I have had in a can. That is not, however, saying much. The few times I have had canned coffee (I generally avoid packaged processed foods) it has tasted oily, as that is what "non-dairy creamer" is, oil, and the coffee itself was pretty nasty.
This coffee, however, is made by a coffee company, and a European gourmet coffee company at that. They know coffee, how to choose, roast and brew it. It is smooth coffee, lightly sweetened, and *without high fructose corn syrup* :) When I am on the road I generally look for bottled water. If that isn't available I get lemonade or juice, choosing canned coffee (or a water fountain) if none of the above is available (I just will not consume most of the additives in canned drinks). This particular coffee, I would bump up in that line, as it is actually more wholesome than most of the packaged lemonade, for example.

I would also describe this more as a medium roast, and am surprised, given that they drink pretty sturdy coffee in Italy, that the company describes it as an espresso. It may be that it is prepared with an espresso roast? But it is definitely milder than what most people would describe as espresso. It is, however, reasonably good coffee, prepared with entirely natural ingredients, and that in itself is almost revelatory!
Arrived soon enough, last for a pretty long time, tastes good and it is good for you. Will buy again.

DISCLAIMER: I have a *BIG* sweet tooth.

I must say that I enjoyed these cookies a lot. There's a nice chocolate coating on the outside that covers a peanut butter flavored creme coated Oreo cookie half. It's just the right ratio of cookie crunch to peanut butter creme to chocolate coating.

My only issue is that these cookies are a tad messy to eat. It's fairly cool where I live right now and I noticed that the outside coating on these was already a little soft even before I picked up a cookie, and then the coating definitely rubbed off on my fingers as I ate the cookies. This isn't an issue if you can wash your hands as soon as you're done eating, but if not -- such as if you snack on these while driving -- you could end up making a mess.

Alright, I'll preface by saying that I have not had the pricing or expiration (not that I would notice) issues that some of the other reviewers have faced. I prefer the 3-pack. I get them every 3 months and the price has always been between 6.50 and 8.50. This is a tremendous bargain. One of these boxes at Duane Reade costs $4.99+. I would probably get it delivered more than once every 3 months if I ate breakfast more.

This is by far my favorite cereal, and while I may sound like a child, I'm 27. Since you're curious, the other members of the Cereal Rushmore are:
Cinnamon Toast Crunch
Frosted Flakes
Corn Pops
Honorable Mention: Lucky Charms

Boom, done.

We ordered this food to try something new with our two small dogs.. One wasn't picky at all and dove right in, while the other refuses to it. It is a very good food however, and I feel good knowing they are getting the nutrition that they need.

Kellogg's Krave cereal has a definite chocolate taste. It's almost like eating a crispy covered truffle. It's no See's or Godiva, but the chocolate center has the flavor and texture of ganache. The outer layer is like a chocolate wafer. The aftertaste is very slightly bitter, not sugary as if you eating real chocolate candies.

This cereal makes a tasty snack dry, but it also stays crispy in milk to the point you would expect cereal to do. My kids like chocolate and view this cereal as a special treat. I'm not sold on eating something so chocolaty for breakfast, but Krave is a cereal I'll eat later in the day.

I assumed from the flavor that this was a fairly sugary and not too nutritious cereal, but I was largely wrong. While chocolate flavored filling and sugar are the first two ingredients, it does have 3 grams of fiber, 2 of protein, and the fat and sodium content aren't too high. I definitely feel better about serving this to my family than the sugary, colorful cereals marketed toward kids. It's not a bad choice for cereals, and may be just the thing to help chocoholics get off to a good start in the morning.

Don't be fooled by other puddings. Sure there's Irish White Pudding, but it's not nearly as thick and long as Irish Black Pudding.
Don't forget. Once you've tried black, you'll never go back!

This dog food has done well for my Alaskan Malamute. We had difficulties with her ability to digest all other foods and are pleased with how this food makes her coat soft, as well as she is able to digest it easily. Recommend to anyone else who is struggling with a sensitive stomach in their dog. Did not give 5 stars due to the price.

When I first saw the jacket photo of this book, I was intrigued by the subtitle/teaser line "It's Morning Somewhere." A pensive, philosophical, thought-provoking line. So imagine my disappointment when the package arrived, and there was no book anywhere to be found... instead, the box was nearly full of what appeared to be sweet-smelling packing flakes.

After also fruitlessly searching for any instruction manual for the product, I was trying to decide what to do next when my daughter came in, gave me a withering look as only a teenager can, and (indicating the picture on the front of the box, showing the packing flakes in a bowl with milk) suggested I just try EATING some.

To my astonishment, this proved very successful. The flakes had a sweet, nutty taste rather like my grandmother's peanut brittle from when I was a kid. The peanutty taste was not really overpowering, and while they WERE noticeably sweet, the sweetness was also not excessive. While I like peanuts and peanut butter, peanut-flavored items like peanut butter cookies are not my personal favorite. Even so, I enjoyed the sweet-nuttiness of this stuff enough to have another bowl or two over the next few days, with just as good results. I think anyone who particularly enjoys peanut-flavored confections (peanut cookies, peanut candies) would enjoy this product even more than I did.

I might also mention that I only got to have a total of two or three bowls of the interesting flakes myself, because my wife and kids proceeded to devour them with great enthusiasm, declaring them yummy.

My doggie always ate his food in one gulp and then let out a HUGE burp after eating because he gulped too fast! Now he is eating MUCH slower because he has to work for it. Product is new, so we have to help him still, but this turns it into an interactive play toy rather than a feeder. He never gets frustrated with it because it is fun for him to drag it around by the rope. Durable, fun for him, easy to fill, but I did think it is a little pricey.
Now if only I can get him to drink his water slower...

This beverage is pretty easy to prepare - just add hot water to the powder and stir. The drink smelled wonderful - a nice spicy ginger with a lingering bit of lemon and just a touch of sweetness. I expected it to taste similar, and was a little disappointed that there seemed to be less lemon flavor than the smell suggested. After a several sips, I decided it was a little spicy for me to enjoy as it was, so I decided to add a couple of lumps of sugar. Sweetening it up a bit made the drink a success for me and I really enjoyed the remainder.

The major downside to this for me is the price. At a little under $4 a box, I will probably opt to stick with a much less expensive ginger tea and add my own lemon. While this drink has no steeping time, I don't mind waiting a few extra minutes to save some money.

The only texture this "conserve" has is jelly like. It appears like juice and pectin. The raspberry taste is there, but you have to use the whole jar (almost) for one piece of toast.
I love St Dalfour's Tea and the Jams. Next time I just won't order "conserves".

We are glad we found this mix as we make pancakes without eggs for my son who has an allergy.
They taste fine for our family- we like them many ways!

Unfortunately, as other reviewers have mentioned, the top loosened during shipping and some leakage did occur. All in all, though, I'm very pleased with this product and would recommend.

Very light for my taste. I mean, I liked it very much, but I would like it a little bit thicker.

I got to try these for free from inluenster.com, and liked them! I tried the banana nut, and it was very moist and made for a great on-the-go breakfast!

I am generally not a huge fan of marshmallow, but I'd heard good things about these, so I decided to give them a try. These are rather sweet, not surprisingly, so I could only eat one at a time. But they are quite good, and one is plenty.

These are very good canned artichoke hearts. I didn't experience any rough or tough heart quarters and the brine isn't too salty. We like this brownie mix and I usually use the low fat recipe on it. I also add chocolate chips or something else to it otherwise it ends up a little bit dry.

We've always enjoyed Snyder's pretzels, so was excited to find they made a gluten free version (recently found out our son is gluten intolerant). They were quite tasty, like a dry pretzel,  it I personally would have preferred a bit more salt.

I am surprised to see so many strong negative reviews for "Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar". Personally, I find the taste to be delicious; it (the taste) is rich in chocolate flavor, while also avoiding the overly-sweet sugar taste that is common with lower-end chocolate confections. "Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar" also manages to minimize the bitter taste that is common for dark chocolate, which is a huge plus for me, considering that I am not a big fan of dark chocolate in the first place.

In all, highly recommended.

This particular brand of squid ink pasta is quite delicious. Nothing beats the real thing but making this pasta is a laborious process.  Trying to find a ready made product is usually an endless search.  Finally, a brand that delivers a smooth pasta with the hint of the sea.

Endorphin Rush is an intense sauce, but it's not one of the better ones. It's ultra hot, but unlike it's contemporaries (such as Blair's Jersey Death or 357 Mad Dog), the tongue's trip to Hell is short lasted. Intense, but not malicious.

As for flavor, this is where Endorphin Rush drives off a cliff. There is no flavor. As a lifelong tea drinker I usually prefer loose tea but on occasion and for convenience sake I make my tea with tea bags. Here are my comments with regards to the Higgins & Burke Earl Grey tea bags:

GENERAL:
1. These tea bags are individually wrapped to preserve their flavor - a plus in my opinion because too many tea bags produce rather bland tasting tea when they just come unprotected in large boxes.
2. When removing the wrapper the tea's scent is pleasant but not overwhelming, quite balanced.
3. It produces a good strong and flavorful cup of tea which is not bitter (I use 1 bag per cup and steep for 3 minutes).
4. According to the manufacturer this tea is produced under Ethical Tea Partnership guidelines.

FLAVOR/SCENT
The flavor of this tea is a bit more on the citrus-y side and does not have as strong a bergamot note as is normally the case with Earl Grey. However, I did not mind this - the flavor was a good balance between a slightly more dominating orange flavor and a subtle but noticeable undertone of bergamot which gave a kind of earthy depth to the orange flavor.

This is a pleasant tea and a slightly different interpretation - at least to my taste buds - of the usual Earl Grey which tends to be heavier on the bergamot. Recommend.

"To decaffeinate using carbon dioxide (CO2), water-softened materials are "pressure cooked" with the gas. At high pressures and high temperatures, carbon dioxide is in a supercritical state, acting as both a gas and a liquid. It becomes a solvent with its small, nonpolar molecules attracting the small caffeine molecules. Since flavor molecules are larger, they remain intact, which is why this process retains the flavor of the material better.". "Caffeine is not removed completely using any of these methods, but under federal regulations in the United States, caffeine levels must not be above 2.5 percent of the product in order for a product to be labeled "decaffeinated."".

I purchased three well reviewed brands of catnip for Tristan, my six month old Savannah cat. In the video, I have just placed down three plates of catnip from freshly opened packages. The brands from left to right are Sojos Certified Organic Catnip, in the middle is the product in this listing - Cosmic Catnip (this video review shows the 3oz jar), and on the far right we have Frontier Catnip Leaf & Flower C/s Certified Organic, 16 Ounce Bag.

Like the little bear at Goldilock's table, Tristan tries a bit from each plate; at the end of this clip he seemed to have no *overwhelming* preference for any particular brand though. As far as his physical reactions to each (sampled separately), he did not act "stoned" nor hyper, he merely scratches on his scratch pad a bit more with catnip than without catnip and gives himself a good stretch. He also strongly prefers catnip infused mice to non-catnip mice and I'm happy to oblige.

As far as which *I* prefer, if it's all the same to the cat (and it seems that it is) here's my take on things -

The Frontier brand is by far the least expensive at just under fifteen dollars for 16oz. It is slightly more coarse and seems to have a little bit of stems mixed in. VERY fragrant though and turned out to be a close second favorite of the cat reviewing the products. I would definitely buy the Frontier brand again and use it for stuffing toys generously or for "marinating" his little cloth mice. Organic and suitable even for human consumption if you like it as a tea.

The Sojos brand (1oz can) is the most expensive - by my calculations comes to over a hundred dollars for 16oz!. The description says it produces a "harmless, euphoric state" but we saw no evidence of that. Smelled fresh but definitely a milder aroma than the other two brands; had the finest chopped leaves of the three. Hand harvested if that is important you or your cat.

With the Cosmic Cat brand, we *may* have a winner.....

When the camera was off, Tristan returned to the Cosmic Cat sample several times more so than the other brands. I repeated this little taste test for the next two days and Cosmic Cat had a small but definite edge over the competition. I'd have to say that I agree with his choice; the Cosmic Cat brand leaves are darker and more fragrant than the other two brands. The leaves are also cut just right - not too fine/not too large, and no stems or coarse pieces. I find the Cosmic Cat brand's price reasonable, the storage container is very convenient, and the 3oz* size is enough not to be too little and not so much to get stale and spoil.

Hope you find this information useful in choosing for your own cat or kitten.

I brewed the coffee using my Capresso 10-cup coffee maker with cold fresh water and a ratio of 1 tablespoon per 6 ounce cup of water.

The coffee brewed with an aroma of coffee and vanilla. The vanilla dominated the brewing smells. First sip of of dark roasted coffee with a hint of vanilla flavor. I like the mild vanilla flavor. I love coffee and I usually don't like flavors masking the flavor of the beans. Roastmasters work hard to perfect their roasts and often times the flavors added destroy that. This is not the case with this coffee. The vanilla flavor augments the roast and adds to it, not takes away from it. The vanilla flavor is also fresher and more natural without the cloying artificial taste often associated with flavored coffee.

My only beef with this coffee and with starbucks in general is that they often over roast their coffees to Italian roasts or beyond the second crack. I find this often masks complexities of the wonderful beans they use and substitute heavy mouthfeel and body for complexity. For that reason, I only give this coffee a four star rating.

Another note is that this coffee seems to have plenty of caffeine. With only a cup or two, I feel the effects quite strongly, which is unusual because of the amount of coffee and tea I drink.

Overall a good flavored coffee. Not overpowering and with a natural hint of vanilla flavor.

Yea, those who claim these bars are not "real" pemmican are right. The original stuff was a mix of dried beef and rendered fat, sometimes with whatever local berries could be found. Even those who ate it regularly hated it. (Mostly voyagers and the like.)
Those who whine that this is not real pemmican are clueless. In 1830 or for that matter 2012, meticulously prepared meat-based pemmican still can go rancid. In fact, it WILL go rancid. It was mostly an emergency fall-back ration.
Better by far were the old Wilson meat bars of the early '70s. The US military still uses something similar in some of their MREs. Sadly I can find no source for the bars any more.
If you make and seal pemmican meticulously with a vacum pump heat sealer they MAY stay eatable for a week in hot weather. I would not count on it. It is also a very pricey item to make, even from scratch.
If you want a meat based product that is close to the original, buy one of hundreds of small shelf stable sausages such as salami, pepperoni, summer sausage, etc. Large groceries handle dozens of varieties. I have even seen low fat varieties such as pepperoni. There are also smaller items like Slim Jims and their fellow travelers for smaller meals or smaller appetites. overall synapsis:

The Pacific Natural Foods Organic Free Range Chix Broth is a very healthy alternative to most of the broth sold on the market(s) and it has a neutral flavor to let one either spice it up and keep it down.

It tastes decent, not especially flavorful when compare to some other brands.

It has lower sodium and than a lot of broths out there but the sea salt gives it a more "salty" taste.

It doesn't use a lot of articificial ingredients other stock/broths put in theirs. Overall, a decent stock for general use.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
(detailed review for those wanting more indepth review)

*note* most stores sell broths (and not stock). So in my review, I often will use "broth" when comparing the stock to other broths(the ones in the supermarkets). Hope this helps :-)

1) Taste:

it is neutral, but we like to add our own ingredients to our own soups anyways. A lot of times other stock/broth have a bit too much onion, garlic, or other spices.

This one is pretty plain in flavor thus it gives the cook/chef a lot more creativity. Because it IS organic and free range, the stock is heartier and heavier than regular watered down, steroid laden chix broths, meaning: it has a bit more "cloudiness" to it than the regular clear chix broth out there.

It does leave a taste behind, not exactly an after taste but a nice finish, per se.

We have used this stock for something as simple as homemade egg drop soup(using little bit of sliced ginger(taken out after cooking), salt to taste, and once the soup heated up, adding some dissolved corn starch, letting it boil again, turned off, then dropping a well beaten egg by drizzling it over the top of the soup to create a flowery effect, the Chinese call it "Egg Flower Soup" vs "Egg Drop Soup") to something as hearty as Minestrone.

It's not very good all by itself as we have served this to our sick children and they can't seem to swallow it plain(myself as well when I was sick) when we just wanted some clear broth.

Without added salt or flavoring, the broth itself is very bland.

It doesn't have a "canned" taste to it and that's a nice plus

2) Size

it is rare to find stocks/broths in this serving size. Most broths come much larger. When I am by myself, I can just open one up without wasting the extras. And Amazon do sell the bigger sizes on the site but when you compare oz to oz, this size is actually slightly cheaper (about .007 cents) than the regular sizes making it the PERFECT serving size! (do bear in mind that prices at Amazon changes all the time.)

3) Packaging

we like the "tetra-pak" packing of this product. It doesn't have a metallic taste to it. It is nicely packed in 4 packs so it stores easily on the shelf without taking up a lot of space. Round cans really waste spaces while these tetra/square packes utilize every inch of the cabinet space.

the only downside to the packaging is that it is NOT recyclable(for us, in our area).

4) Does it "groove?" (make gravy)

Why this matters...

a lot of folks like to make gravies with their broth. And we have been asked by our friends quite a bit why we prefer to use stocks vs. broths when it comes to making gravy.

For those that are interested:

there is a bit of difference between stock and broth. Stock are bones/marrow cooked thus more gelatinous, broth are meat prepped so it doesn't have gelatin to it. This makes a difference when one wants to make something thick like gravy.

a good gravy requires a bit of help from the stock itself, to gelatinize, and while one can make gravy with broth, stocks are superior when it comes to making things such as gravies.

This stock, however, doesn't make gravy well for some reason. Not sure why. We've tested it a few times, it requires much more flour than the conventional recipes. So bare that in mind if you want to make gravy with the this stock. On the other hand, I'd highly recommend the stock made by "wolfgang Puck" it is a better stock both in flavor and "grooving" ability. LOL

5) Odds and Ends

this broth is a good and healthy alternative to those that like lower sodium options and do not like a lot of flavoring to their soup. What makes it even better is not just that it is organic, but free range.

By definition, organic means that the chickens are not fed hormones and are fed natural grains, but that doesn't mean that they can roam free, they might still be caged up in a limited space. Free range means the chicken can roam more freely(although some farmers have argued that chicken that can have 10 feet of range is consider free range, it is still better than being couped up in a 3" X 3" square with their beaks cut off and being injected by nothing but steroids). A chicken that can roam is definitely a healthier chicken. They produce more muscular meat and healthier bones and we get to benefit from that.

We have switched to as much free range chicken as we could afford while at least all organic and have seen a good healthy change in our bodies along with other diets and exercises.

I would also recommend having Wolfgang Pucks Organic Chicken Broth and chicken stock on hand (they sell it here on Amazon). The Wolfgang Puck brand stock is more flavorful and stands more on its own and creates recipes that are more flavorful.

We use this product whenever we want to serve something more neutral when pairing with other more flavorful foods.

On a sick day, the Wolfgang Puck BROTH is superior by itself. (in plain taste, we prefer broths over stocks, the Wolfgang Puck's broth is excellent by itself!)

But we still like this product a lot, for its healthy and neutral taste thus giving us a lot of room for creativity

*note* some of the folks have complained that it is too salty while others stated that it is low sodium. I personally think everyone's taste buds are different and I have cooked for folks for dinner at the same time that would say my dishes are too salty to not salty at all. I think some of that has to do with the way we grow up, the way our genetics are, and our age and habits.

If a person has cut down on their salt intake for a period of time, their taste buds will be more sensitive to salt.

In this case, sea salt is a very strong salt. Using just a pinch of it can equal to the 30 times the taste of the table spoon salt. But the sodium level is still lower because less salt is used.

I can see why some folks would say it tastes too salty while others say it is not that salty.

To me and my wife, our salt intake tend to be on the higher end so this broth doesn't taste "salty" to us. Hope this helps.

****totally unimportant view****

btw, no matter how healthy or good the broth is for humans, it is always bad for the chicken(s)themselves: organic, free range, or caged...makes one wonder if they'd ever think: "maybe we shouldn't cross the road...because the butcher is on the other side..."
